457	**A repair evidence requirement over one of these two relations has its own
458	owning outcome law**, `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law`
459	(§6). It is separate from native §4.6 because these relations mint no `fact2` and
460	carry no Coverage, and **each kind is projected through its own payload**: a
461	runtime requirement reads `observability`, `observationWindow` and
462	`observedPopulation`; a history requirement reads `revisionRange` and
463	`collectionScope`, which are its bounds fields; `HistoryPayloadV1` also carries
464	subjects and has no runtime observation-window, population or observability
465	fields. Neither kind may report the other's outcomes.
466	
467	**A repair target is a fingerprint, not a path, and the join is published.**
468	`RepairPlanDescriptor.targets` are `finding-key2:` **fingerprints**, while
469	`RuntimeSubject` is keyed by `{path, symbol?}` and `HistorySubject` by `{path}`.
470	The deterministic projection is
471	`imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-imported-requirement-law/targetSubjectProjection`:
472	each target must be a finding of the evidence Run named by `evidenceRunId` (preview
473	already refuses one that is not); that `finding-key2` identity is the H identity of
474	the retained foundation `finding-fingerprint` descriptor, whose retention is
475	`preimage` and whose bytes are therefore re-hashed at Run closure; and its
476	`subjectKey` supplies the path and qualified name used for matching. The projection
477	does not classify the target by `kind`, whose vocabulary is not closed here. A
478	runtime row matches on path and, if it names a symbol, on qualified name; another
479	symbol's row does not match. A runtime row with no symbol and every history row
480	provide **file** granularity, with `granularityWidenedToFile` disclosed in the
481	projection and successful outcome. A symbol-naming runtime row provides the
482	format's path-and-name granularity, not an exact match of the whole subject key:
483	neither format distinguishes `language`, `kind` or `discriminator`. Distinct
484	findings can therefore project to the same observation. This stated limit applies
485	to every such projection; it cannot establish execution or non-execution of a
486	particular subject variant beyond the captured granularity. More than one
487	matching subject **refuses**: an ambiguous projection is not resolved by choosing
488	one. A target with no matching subject is unsupported — never satisfied, and never
489	read as evidence of non-use.
490	
491	Five limits carry over and are enforced rather than assumed.
492	**Satisfied does not mean positive**: `observed-hit` is positive execution
493	evidence and `observable-unhit` is *bounded negative* evidence, both can satisfy,
494	and the disclosure records which did. **No imported observation establishes a
495	universal negative** — one window is not universal non-use — and imported evidence
496	can never *by itself* establish the native closed world or authorize an unsafe
497	`delete`/`replace`, and it can never **improve** that gate either: the gate reads
498	only the **native** `ClosedWorldV2` records the §6 relevance rule selects from the
499	evidence Run, and no imported observation is one of them.
500	It may still be an **additional required condition** alongside an
501	already-established native basis, so it is wrong to say it never affects
502	applicability; an unsatisfied imported requirement makes an otherwise-eligible
503	plan inapplicable. **Whole-versus-partial** is decided by the requirement's
504	`completeness` field: `complete` needs every plan target supported,
505	`partial-acceptable` at least one. That enum already existed, but **this reading of
506	it for an imported requirement over plan targets is selected here** and was not
507	previously published. A target that is unobservable or outside the history
508	collection scope therefore only names the cause *more precisely when the support
509	test fails* — it does not veto a lawful `partial-acceptable` requirement that has a
510	supported target. **Bounds are separate from support**: an insufficient observation
511	window or revision range applies under both completeness values, because it is a
512	property of the observation rather than of the target count. And **required versus
513	optional** stays where `evidenceUse` puts it — an optional absence remains the
514	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` disclosure and is satisfied *by absence* rather than
515	by evidence. That declaration reaches the requirement boundary as a **typed
516	boolean**; a non-boolean refuses, so there is no `unknown` state to default and no
517	falsy value is read as optional.
518	
519	---
520	
521	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
522	
523	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV2` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
524	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
525	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
526	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
527	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
528	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
529	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
530	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
531	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
532	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
533	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
534	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
535	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
536	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
537	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
538	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
539	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
540	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
541	
542	Glob matching follows the single [portable glob contract](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/glob-pattern-contract.v1.md): full-string, case-sensitive matching; terminal whole-segment `**` includes a filename, so `src/**` matches `src/index.ts`. The same predicate applies to policy field filters and host path scopes. Each containing contract continues to own its defaults and include/exclude combination law.
543	The compiled RuleProgramV2 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
544	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
545	The exact endpoint, native field projection and imported test-filter grammars
546	are in that policy schema and the incorporated atom contract. Identity §4 and
547	the composition contract own independent subject enumeration, complete tree
548	replay, full finding emission, waiver membership and budget semantics. Declared
549	required evidence remains distinct from retained nonblocking branch diagnostics.
550	
551	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
552	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
553	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
554	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
555	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
556	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
557	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly.
558	
559	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. A suite supplies the
560	candidate policy, waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only overrides and cases with
561	typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage, available evidence kinds) or
562	a bounded source fixture. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
563	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
564	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers); sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
565	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
566	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
567	The result (`policytest2:`) records candidate and effective digests, resolver
568	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
569	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
570	
571	**Candidate → inspect → review (Map side).** `opensip candidates` lists
572	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds
573	(`clone-candidate`, `low-confidence-unused`, `runtime-unhit`, `history-stale`) with an
574	evidence level. Only a finding on a gating rule is `controlBearing`. `opensip inspect`
575	returns a bounded `InspectionBundle` (≤ 4096 facts, Coverage, imports, limitations).
576	`opensip review join` records a `ReviewDisposition` (`accept|reject|defer`, reviewer
577	principal human/model/policy-rule, note, `suppressUntil` ≤ 365 days) as a mutation
578	with a receipt. The disposition schema admits no verdict, Run, baseline or
579	authorization field: review can never mint a Control verdict or authorize a repair.
580	`reject`/`defer` suppress the candidate from listings until `suppressUntil` or until
581	its fingerprint changes; expired suppressions resurface with `previouslyReviewed`.
582	`opensip review brief` is an advisory, bounded (≤ 1000) ordering labelled with its
583	producer (a model producer names its `closure2`); truncation is explicit.
584	
585	---
586	
587	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
588	
589	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
590	
591	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
592	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
593	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
594	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
595	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
596	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
597	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
598	`run3`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
599	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
600	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
601	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
602	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
603	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
604	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.
605	
606	**The closed-world gate reads selected native records; the descriptor carries a
607	display summary.** The guard covers **every `delete` and every `replace` edit** in
608	the plan — the unsafe-action set is those two actions, without qualification, and
609	this paragraph narrows it in no way. If the plan contains one, the prerequisite is
610	decided **before** any descriptor is built, and an `imported-prepared-declared`
611	evidence origin reports `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` for the separate
612	reason that a DECLARED prepared expansion is not authority for an unsafe repair.
613	
614	**A Run holds one `ClosedWorldV2` per Coverage entry, not one per Run, so the gate
615	states which entries it reads.** `ClosedWorldV2` is a required member of
616	`ViewEntryV3` (native §4.3), keyed by `CoverageKeyV2`
617	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`,
618	`subjectScopeCommitment`), and identity §3 makes several differing entries lawful
619	in one Run: "a differing tuple is a different claim, not an overlap, which is why
620	the same subject may lawfully appear under two relations, two rungs or two
621	universes." An earlier revision of this section said the prerequisite was decided
622	against "the evidence Run's own native `ClosedWorldV2`", as though a Run held one.
623	It does not, and with several retained records that phrase did not denote. The
624	selection law is the following, and it is decided over **retained** records only.
625	
626	1. **Relevant universes.** The relevant set is the union of two published joins,
627	   and a universe in neither is **truly unrelated and does not veto**.
628	   * Every universe reached by **all matching occurrences of every target
629	     fingerprint**: `finding3.subjectId` → `subject3.universe`. All occurrences,
630	     not a representative — a `finding-key2` frame carries no universe, and the
631	     projection law that groups occurrences compares `ruleId`, subject path,
632	     kind, qualified name and detector closure but **not** universe, so one
633	     fingerprint may lawfully be matched in two universes.
634	   * Every universe that **owns an unsafe edited path**, read from the
635	     **retained selected-program census** of this Run's `EnumerationPlanV1`. That
636	     parameter is **required** for evaluator3 — absent, the evaluator refuses
637	     `EVALUATOR_REQUIRED_PARAMETER_MISSING`, and full replay re-admits it — so this
638	     is a guaranteed retained join, not a caller-selected or optional unsigned map
639	     and not filename parsing. For each binding whose `enumerator.status` is
640	     `selected`, its **applicable path census** is its own `extents[]` plus, on a
641	     candidate-only cell, its `candidateSourcePaths` — "the Plan-selected
642	     source-path census for *that* program".
643	     - A binding with a **non-null universe** whose census contains the path
644	       contributes that universe.
645	     - A **selected but unavailable** binding (`universe=null`, whose `extents`
646	       remain "populated from host membership so expected file/package paths are
647	       not lost") contributes **typed unresolved ownership**: it holds a real
648	       retained expected-ownership claim with no universe to make eligible and no
649	       Coverage to establish a closed world, so it reports
650	       `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` and **does not vanish because some
651	       other owner of the same path is closed**.
652	     - An **unselected** binding is not a selected program and is never inferred.
653	     Each extent kind is read as itself: `file` and `package` are host membership
654	     extents, `symbol` is the selected program's **code** scope. All snapshot files
655	     are therefore **not** treated as every compiler's `programRootFiles`, and a
656	     selected program whose own census does not contain the edit **stays
657	     unrelated**. Legitimate **multiple ownership is preserved** — one path
658	     analysed under two Rust targets or editions is two selected bindings with two
659	     universes, and both must be eligible.
660	   * Retained **`source-path`** subject scopes (`file`, `clones`, `vcs-change`,
661	     all `universeRule: same-only`) are unioned in as an **additional retained
662	     witness**. They are **not** the owner census and cannot certify its
663	     completeness: their `subjectKindLaw` proves those scopes *name* paths, not
664	     that they *enumerate* every selected program owning one. A selected program
665	     with no such scope in this Run owns its extent just the same — which is
666	     exactly the case the census covers, and which is reachable: a universe bound
667	     only to a symbol-kind cell, owning a path through its retained symbol extent
668	     with no file inventory and no lawful `file@enumerated` scope, is admitted.
669	     Ownership is never inferred from a path prefix, a display string, an optional
670	     sidecar or an unreferenced host observation, and never by reconstructing a
671	     path from an opaque native symbol ID — that reconstruction is separately
672	     forbidden, and the census makes it unnecessary, because the program's path
673	     extent is published directly.
674	   * Targets and edits are **separate descriptor arrays with no published
675	     correspondence**, and none is invented: each is read on its own terms and
676	     the two universe sets are unioned. No edit names a target.
677	   * If an unsafe edited path is claimed by **no** selected binding's census and
678	     **no** source-path scope, its analysing universe cannot be reconstructed, and
679	     that is reported as `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED` rather than guessed
680	     or treated as vacuously satisfied.
681	2. **Selected records.** For every relevant universe, **every** retained native
682	   `coverage2` of that Run whose scope's **`sourceUniverse`** is that universe.
683	   `ClosedWorldV2` characterises the universe whose subjects were examined —
684	   `coverageTotality.matchLaw` calls totality "a claim about what THIS universe
685	   examined" — and that extent is the scope's source side, so relevance is decided
686	   on `sourceUniverse` **alone**. An entry made in an unrelated universe *about* a
687	   relevant one describes the unrelated universe and is not joined. Selection is
688	   **independent of the plan's `evidenceRequirements`**: a recipe can neither
689	   narrow it to a favourable relation or rung nor remove a conflicting record from
690	   it. Records are deduplicated by retained `coverage2` **identity**, never by
691	   relation, and **ordered on UTF-8 encoded bytes** by
692	   `relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`,
693	   `subjectScopeCommitment`, then the `coverage2` identity — that sixth member
694	   makes the order total even between two records agreeing on all five
695	   coordinates, so remedies are reproducible whatever order the caller enumerated
696	   in.
697	3. **The gate.** Eligibility is the **conjunction** of `deadCodeRepairEligible`
698	   over every selected record. It is **non-vacuous**: a relevant universe that
699	   retains no native Coverage record establishes no closed world, and an empty
700	   evidence subset is not truth — it reports
701	   `REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED`. Each dissenting record contributes its
702	   own remedy naming **all six ordering members unabbreviated** — including the
703	   exact retained `coverage2` identity — plus that record's own `reasons`. Naming
704	   only relation, rung and source universe would not do: two lawfully distinct
705	   retained records can differ **only** in `targetUniverse`, only in
706	   `subjectScopeCommitment`, or only in the identity itself, and a remedy that
707	   cannot tell them apart does not name the record the reader must go and look at.
708	   So two causes remain two remedies, and two records remain two records. The
709	   conservatism is deliberate: a destructive edit is a universal negative, so one
710	   dissenting relevant record defeats it, and the scoping in step 1 is what stops
711	   an unrelated closed finding from justifying the deletion of a path analysed in
712	   an open universe.
713	
714	No new public detail code is minted: every outcome above reports the existing
715	`REPAIR.CLOSED_WORLD_NOT_ESTABLISHED`, and the closed registry is unchanged.
716	
717	`dynamicDispatch` is **not** a global veto and must not be read as one. Native
718	§4.5 makes dynamic-edge effects **target-relative**: `affected_targets` marks the
719	subjects a dynamic edge could reach, and §4.6 turns that into
720	`resolution-incomplete` for a universal negative **about an affected subject**.
721	So a present dynamic edge disqualifies the claims that depend on the subjects it
722	reaches; it does not by itself disqualify an unrelated target in the same Run.
723	The selection law above does not read `dynamicDispatch` at all: a selected record
724	whose `dynamicDispatch` is `present` neither defeats the boolean gate nor changes
725	the display summary, and the member stays with the native record for the
726	target-relative and per-requirement judgements that own it. Those judgements are
727	**separate** from this gate and are not merged into it.
728	The roles here are distinct and are not merged: preview **admits** each evidence
729	requirement's `relation`/`minResolution` against the registered vocabulary and its
730	relation's own ladder (`admit_atom`, which is vocabulary admission, not an
731	evidence judgement), and then **consumes** that requirement's own `satisfied`
732	value; the semantic sufficiency behind it is owned by native §4.6
733	`sufficiency_v2` and the §4.5 affected-target evidence, per requirement, and is
734	never collapsed into one flag.
735	
736	**Which vocabulary `EvidenceRequirement.deficiency` carries, and when it is
737	required.** Preview admits a requirement over **either evidence plane**, so the
738	field carries the vocabulary of **that requirement's** plane and the plane is
739	decided at admission from the relation's registry membership — the same place the
740	two planes are already separated — never from the value.

928	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
929	
930	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
931	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
932	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
933	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
934	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
935	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
936	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
937	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
938	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
939	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
940	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
941	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
942	
943	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
944	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
945	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
946	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). The mandatory sentence before spawn is
947	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
948	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
949	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
950	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
951	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
952	are the supported alternative.

135	## 1. Supported native cells (AR-13)
136	
137	### 1.1 Cell coordinates
138	
139	A cell is `capability × languageMode × platformFamily`. The machine-readable
140	matrix is `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json`, validated by
141	`NativeCapabilityMatrixV2`; its `cells` array is the **complete product** of its
142	own `capabilities` and `languageModes`, and the reference checks hold it to
143	exactly that product rather than to a number written here. (A literal count in
144	this prose said `60` while the matrix held 66; a second hand-maintained counter
145	would only go stale again, so the count is derived from the two arrays and
146	reported by the checks instead of restated.) Platform families are exactly the
147	four `platformId`
148	values in the delivery release inventory: `linux-x86_64-gnu`,
149	`linux-aarch64-gnu`, `macos-aarch64`, `macos-x86_64`. The OS/kernel/libc/filesystem
150	*baseline* that qualifies a machine into a family is owned by the security unit
151	(AR-06); this contract states only that native capabilities are platform-invariant
152	by design (`platformInvariantDesign: true`) and that no cell is `QUALIFIED` here.
153	
154	Cell states (closed): `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` (contracted behavior, corpus named,
155	qualification pending), `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` (refuses with the named deficiency;
156	never silently narrows), `NOT-SELECTED` (outside D-371; no promise).

158	### 1.2 Language modes (closed)
159	
160	| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
161	|---|---|---|---|
162	| `ts-tsconfig` | `tsconfig.json` at the unit root (or named by discovery), `allowJs` absent/false | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=tsconfig` | JavaScript files are not program roots; a JS import target is `unresolved-module-specifier`. |
163	| `js-allowjs` | `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` with effective `allowJs=true` (jsconfig defaults `allowJs=true`) | `typescript-v2`, `allowJs=true` | `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` are program roots. |
164	| `js-synthesized` | Inside a `tsjs` unit already discovered by §1.4 U-1: no `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` at the unit root, so the `package.json` marker selects this mode. `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` files under that unit are program roots; they do not themselves make a unit | `typescript-v2`, `configOrigin=synthesized`, `synthesizerVersion=1` | Host synthesizes `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` (§2.2); Plan-bound with `DEFAULTED` provenance, disclosed in output. |
165	| `rust-cargo` | `Cargo.toml` at the unit root (package or workspace) | `rust-v2` | Requires a sealed `DependencySourceSetV1` when the lock lists any non-path package (§3). |
166	| `rust-cargo-prepared` | as above, plus an admitted `PreparedOutputSetV3` of inert rows | `rust-v2` with `preparedOutputSetId` non-null | Expansions and directives are consumed as data; a site without a row is an unresolved edge (§3.6). |
167	| `syntax-only` | any file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar | `syntax-v2` (grammar-only; no compiler) | Inventory/syntax/clones only; semantic rungs `language-tier-unsupported`. |
168	
169	**This table selects a MODE; it does not discover units.** No Recognition cell
170	mints a unit. For the five rows that name a **compilation** universe —
171	`ts-tsconfig`, `js-allowjs`, `js-synthesized`, `rust-cargo` and
172	`rust-cargo-prepared` — the cell is read **after** §1.4 U-1 has yielded a unit of
173	that language family, because those modes describe a program and a program needs
174	one. **`syntax-only` carries no such prerequisite and must not be read as if it
175	did:** it is the compiler-free path, it has no compilation unit at all (§1.2's
176	third-universe paragraph and §6.3's grammar dialect branch both depend on that),
177	and it is exactly what serves a repository in which U-1 yields **no** TS or Rust
178	unit. A file reached that way is `syntax-only` membership with `unitOrdinal: null`
179	under U-4, not a member of an invented unit. U-1 is the specific model — the closed `WorkspaceUnitV2` record,
180	the exactly-once `FileMembershipRowV1` law and the marker precedence
181	`tsconfig.json` > `jsconfig.json` > `package.json` — and a `tsjs` unit exists only
182	where a directory holds one of those three markers. So a directory of bare `.js`
183	files with no marker is **not** a unit: under U-4 each such file is
184	`syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language`, never a program member,
185	and no `js-synthesized` program is minted for them. An
186	earlier wording of the `js-synthesized` row read as an independent recognition
187	test ("`package.json` present **or** any `.js` file under the unit"), and an
188	implementer taking it alone would have minted units for bare-`.js` directories,
189	changing unit membership and therefore the Plan. The disjunct was never reachable
190	under U-1 — with no `tsconfig.json`, no `jsconfig.json` and no `package.json`
191	there is no unit for a `.js` file to be "under" — and the cell now says what it
192	always meant: within a U-1 unit whose marker is `package.json`, `.js` files are
193	program roots.
194	
195	**The syntax-only universe (CB3-MUST-3).** This column previously read
196	"none (syntax-all provider)", and that made the mode's own advertised cells
197	unrepresentable. `fact2` and `subject-scope` both **require** a
198	`native-semantic-universe` h-identity, that domain set held exactly the
199	TypeScript and Rust universes, and there is no null branch — so a
200	`declares@syntactic` or `clones@normalized-body-hash` fact in `syntax-only`
201	mode, and every `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` fact in a repository containing
202	no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all, could mint no fact and no scope. An
203	implementer had to invent a third domain, invent a null branch on a required
204	identity field, or quietly narrow this table.
205	
206	The registered answer is a third universe, `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2`,
207	over a third native context, `native.context.syntax.v2`. Making the universe
208	fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact
209	states what produced it, and would leave "which grammar read this body"
210	unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on the answer.
211	
212	- **What it carries.** The context holds one thing: the installed
213	  `SyntaxGrammarBundleV1`, pinned the way a toolchain is — an admitted
214	  `kind=grammar` closure, a `parserVersion` that must equal that closure
215	  manifest's `semanticVersion`
216	  (`native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest`), and every grammar
217	  definition, the bundle manifest and the normalizer specification present in
218	  the retained tree. It has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no
219	  `node_modules` layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis
220	  reads none of them. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would assert
221	  semantics the mode never computes.
222	- **What the universe commits.** The admitted context plus the **selected**
223	  grammar set. Selecting a different set is a different universe, exactly as
224	  selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is
225	  visible to every consumer instead of being an invisible default. A selection
226	  naming a grammar the bundle does not contain refuses
227	  (`native.syntax-grammar-not-in-bundle`). The constant
228	  `resolutionAttempted=false` is carried so no consumer can read the universe
229	  as a resolution claim.
230	- **The body dialect axis.** `body-language-version.dialect` gains a third
231	  branch, `{grammarVariant}`. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so
232	  it has no edition to select and no program to join; claiming `{edition: 2021}`
233	  for a `.rs` body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics. One
234	  suffix must map to one grammar
235	  (`native.syntax-grammar-suffix-ambiguous`), longest match wins, and a suffix
236	  with no bundled grammar refuses rather than being folded into a neighbour —
237	  which is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest
238	  classification. Because it is a distinct branch, **a grammar-parsed body never
239	  mints the same identity as a compiler-parsed one over the same bytes.** That
240	  is required: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different
241	  interpretations, and equating them would be a false clone claim.
242	- **Capability is not widened.** A `syntax-only` universe carries only the
243	  inventory rungs, the `syntactic` rungs and `clones@normalized-body-hash`.
244	  `imports`/`references`/`calls`/`types`/`reachability` remain
245	  `language-tier-unsupported` under it, `unresolved-edge` stays unavailable
246	  because no resolution was attempted, and a universal-negative predicate still
247	  requires its own complete `CoverageResultV3`. Nothing here lets a syntax-only
248	  Run claim a resolved or type fact.
249	- **The bundled grammar set is closed, and it has SEVEN languages.** The host
250	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
251	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
252	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
253	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
254	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
255	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
256	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
257	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
258	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
259	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
260	
261	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
262	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
263	
264	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
265	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
266	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
267	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
268	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
269	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
270	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
271	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
272	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
273	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
274	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
275	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
276	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
277	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
278	
279	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
280	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
281	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
282	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
283	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
284	languages instead of ignoring four.
285	
286	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
287	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
288	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
289	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
290	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
291	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
292	
293	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
294	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
295	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
296	
297	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
298	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
299	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
300	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored
301	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
302	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
303	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
304	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
305	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
306	whether facts happen to exist:
307	
308	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
309	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
310	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
311	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
312	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
313	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`). **Inventory capabilities are exempt
314	  here as well as at the scope boundary below** — the exemption belongs to the
315	  *relation*, not to the boundary. An earlier revision wrote this bullet as an
316	  unconditional every-anchor rule and stated the exemption only in the scope
317	  bullet, so the two bullets contradicted each other: a literal implementer
318	  refused a `file@enumerated` fact for `tool/main.py` while the scope bullet had
319	  just promised that the same path's inventory Coverage was unconditionally
320	  `complete` — an inventoried file that is authoritatively absent. An inventory
321	  fact is not read by a grammar at all; it *is* the inventory row, the manifest
322	  declaration or the VCS observation, so there is no grammar for it to be gated
323	  on. (The relation registry's `anchorLaw` independently gives the inventory
324	  class **zero** anchors, so such a fact names no anchor path for this bullet to
325	  test either; the two laws agree and neither leans on the other.) The exemption
326	  is from grammar ownership **only**: the relation's snapshot joins, own-scope
327	  attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes
328	  admissible because some other anchor in the Run sits on a supported path.
329	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
330	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
331	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
332	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
333	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
334	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
335	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
336	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
337	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
338	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
339	  exactly as the matrix already says.
340	
341	**A promised inventory capability represents every inventoried path, and a
342	`complete` inventory result may not hide an omitted one.** These are two halves
343	of one promise and the second was missing. `file@enumerated` is **total** over
344	the snapshot inventory: a snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so
345	every inventoried path has exactly one `file` fact, and over a **complete**
346	`file@enumerated` Coverage the predicate `exists file where path=P` is
347	authoritative. A complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject
348	therefore asserts that an inventoried file is absent, and that graph closed —
349	nothing derived the obligation, so nothing compared it. A `complete`
350	`file@enumerated` Coverage must now carry an admitted `file@enumerated` fact for
351	every one of its subjects that the snapshot inventory contains
352	(`COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH`), derived at Run closure from the
353	retained view's own facts and the retained inventory.
354	
355	**A fact discharges the obligation of the scope it actually belongs to.** The
356	match is on every coordinate the registry's `matchOn` lists — the four
357	`CoverageKeyV2` coordinates other than the commitment itself
358	(`relation`, `resolution`, `sourceUniverse`, `targetUniverse`) plus the owning
359	`snapshotId`. Matching relation and rung *alone* is not enough in a view carrying
360	more than one universe, and this is not hypothetical: the view-level fact/scope
361	join is **existential** — each fact need only agree with *some* scope on relation,
362	rung and both universes — so a TypeScript `file` fact is lawfully present in a
363	view that also carries a syntax-universe `file@enumerated` scope, and while the
364	match was two-coordinate it *paid that scope's missing-file obligation*. A
365	complete Run exhibited exactly that: two `complete` scopes over `a.ts`, only the
366	TypeScript fact, admitted. Totality is a claim about what **this** universe
367	examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in this universe; a fact
368	from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes, not the
369	same observation. The two-universe Run in which *each* scope carries its own fact
370	remains lawful and is retained as a positive control. `snapshotId` is listed
371	although Run closure already forces it on every fact and scope: this law reads one
372	scope's obligation out of a *shared* view, and a join that silently leans on an
373	invariant enforced elsewhere is the same implicit coupling that produced the
374	cross-universe defect.
375	
376	Two things the law deliberately does not require: a subject the snapshot does
377	**not** contain is owed nothing —
378	the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent, which is the
379	one case a universal negative over inventory exists to serve — and an `unknown`
380	result carrying its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing, which keeps a
381	partially examined inventory representable rather than forcing a false
382	`complete`. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are **not**
383	total and owe nothing: most paths declare no package and most were not changed,
384	so their empty results are ordinary findings. Which relations owe totality is
385	stated in the relation registry (`coverageTotality`), where only `file` has a
386	row, and never inferred. This is the specific rule that identity §3's "partition
387	the claimed universe without overlaps or omissions" defers to: the **disjointness**
388	half is general, applies within the full owning
389	`(snapshotId, relation, resolution, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse)` tuple, and is
390	decided at retained Run closure against the registry's own
391	`coveragePartitionLaw`; the **omission** half is discharged only where this
392	registry carries a `coverageTotality` row. For the nine `symbol`-kind relations it
393	carries none, and the reason is the trust boundary stated below — symbol-to-file
394	attribution is not re-derivable from the retained Run — so no fact-per-symbol
395	obligation exists there. Evaluator3 separately requires the selected symbol
396	inventory and accounts for required work over its independently retained census
397	(identity §4). A symbol may have no call/reference fact, while a whole expected
398	inventory or work partition cannot silently disappear. Disjointness still applies, because it
399	asks a different question: not what was examined, but whether one interpretation
400	claimed a subject twice.

19	## S1. Authority, applicability and superseded selectors
20	
21	The first-party host is the only authority for discovery, trust time, root
22	chain acceptance, revocation, platform admission, migration and leases. Content
23	identity never proves custody. A signed document proves only that its signer
24	signed those bytes; whether the document is admitted is decided by the rules
25	below, evaluated at the host's trust instant. Detector compatibility listings
26	inherit tree, platform and protocol from the already-admitted `closure2`, not
27	from fields on the listing body. Identity §3 hashes `closure2` over `{kind,
28	manifestDigest, tree, semanticVersion, protocolMajor, platform}` and states that
29	a component manifest for a different tree, platform or selected component is
30	refused by delivery admission. That delivery selector is DR-103
31	`component-manifest-schemas.v11` `manifestSchema.platforms[]` (`os`, `arch`,
32	`tree` TreeCommitment, `entrypoint`) together with RJ-3, not `DetectorManifestV1`.
33	Authenticated association of those component-manifest bytes is the existing
34	envelope (`opensip-signature-envelope.2` subject `kind=manifest`, domain
35	`opensip.metadata.manifest.1`, `storedSha256` equal to identity
36	`closure.manifestDigest` raw-artifact) plus catalog `opensip-catalog.1`
37	`releases[]` `{manifestDigest, manifestPreimageSha256, envelopeDigest,
38	artifacts[{platform, archiveProfileId, archiveDigest, sha256}]}` signed TR-INDEX.
39	Workflows-and-surfaces §2 then admits **that** `closure2` from a retained
40	generation, an installed signed release with the same `closure2`, or a signed
41	`closureBundle`. Identity `closure.tree` projects that selected platform
42	TreeCommitment onto regular files only: each `type=file` entry maps to one
43	identity `Blob` `{path, sha256, bytes}` with the same path string,
44	`sha256=entry.sha256`, `bytes=entry.length`, and retained blob length matching
45	(`BLOB_LENGTH`); `type=dir` and `type=symlink` stay delivery rows, are not
46	identity Blob members, and are never followed into a listing (RJ-3 keeps
47	symlink targets inside the tree). Mode bits remain on the TreeCommitment row
48	and are not identity members; listing bytes are never executed. `DetectorManifestV1`
49	is only `{schemaFamily, schemaMajor, compatibleClosures}` (`additionalProperties`
50	false); it cannot be the component-manifest preimage and must not occupy
51	`closure.manifestDigest`. The listing is the optional unique reserved regular-file
52	path `.opensip/detector-compatibility.json` in that already-admitted same
53	`closure2` tree (exact NFC path; not the project-host `.opensip/project-id.v1`
54	custody marker). Path absent is no declaration; empty `compatibleClosures` is a
55	complete declaration; a present path that is not `type=file`, whose
56	Blob/length/digest disagrees with the TreeCommitment file row, or whose retained
57	bytes fail the existing W listing schema, refuses and does not downgrade. Tree,
58	path or digest swap fails closure or delivery admission; catalog digest match
59	alone never admits. After that association the host projects a closed receipt
60	`{closureId, componentManifestDigest, listing, trustOrigin, compatibleClosures,
61	tree, platform, protocolMajor}` only when the reserved file is present and
62	valid. `listing` is its exact Blob `{path, sha256, bytes}`;
63	`componentManifestDigest` is the admitted closure's `manifestDigest`, and
64	`trustOrigin` is `retained-generation` | `installed-signed-release` |
65	`signed-closure-bundle`. The other fields copy the same admitted closure and
66	listing. Path absence produces no compatibility projection; an empty listing
67	produces a projection with `compatibleClosures: []`. This is not a second
68	signature verifier, listing schema or `signatureVerified` flag. Workflow
69	`host.closures[].trust='admitted'` is a TCB fixture assumption, the same class

106	
107	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
108	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
109	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
110	
111	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
112	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
113	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
114	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
115	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
116	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
117	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
118	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
119	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
120	
121	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
122	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
123	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
124	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
125	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
126	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
127	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
128	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
129	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
130	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
131	
132	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
133	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
134	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
135	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
136	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
137	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
138	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
139	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
140	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
141	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
142	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
143	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
144	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
145	
146	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
147	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
148	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
149	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
150	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
151	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
152	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
153	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
154	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
155	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
156	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
157	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.

164	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one

324	## S4. Trust time (AR-04)
325	
326	Definitions. `evalHighWater` (floor F): highest instant at which a decision
327	evaluation was made. `lastAccepted` (L): issue time of the newest accepted
328	signed document; required whenever F exists. **Admitted time evidence** A =
329	max(L, accepted witness time, presented root issue time), where a witness is
330	the newest issue time of a presented payload whose signature already verified
331	and which is not older than L. The wall clock is untrusted.
332	
333	Decision evaluation, in order, for record R, observation (wall W, sleep-
334	inclusive monotonic M, bootId B), optional payload P:
335	
336	1. Payload future check (unchanged FC-FUTURE): an issue time > W + 24 h refuses
337	   `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`; nothing is written.
338	2. Fresh install (F absent): without admitted time evidence the evaluation
339	   refuses `TRUST.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT` (the core's embedded bootstrap
340	   payload or an ordinary payload is required); nothing is written. With it,
341	   W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` and initialises nothing.
342	   Otherwise tEval = max(W, A); F := tEval, L := A, anchor := (B, M, W); expiry
343	   states are evaluated from the presented documents, never set to false.
344	3. In-session continuity: if the anchor has the same bootId, expected =
345	   anchorWall + (M − anchorMono). A forward deviation over 24 h refuses
346	   `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD` (`in-session`) unless a witness proves the
347	   expectation itself was behind (witness ≥ expected). A backward deviation is
348	   the finding `CLOCK-REGRESSION-IN-SESSION`; a monotonic value below the
349	   anchor's is `CLOCK-CONTINUITY-MALFORMED` (finding, anchor not rewritten).
350	4. Plausibility: W > A + 90 d refuses `CLOCK-EXCURSION-FORWARD`
351	   (`beyond-horizon`) **before any evaluation and before any write**. Remedy:
352	   correct the clock, or present a payload issued within 90 d of W.
353	5. Evaluation: tEval = max(F, W, A). The floor written is exactly tEval
354	   (write-ahead, §5.6 durability), so the persisted floor and the evaluated
355	   instant never differ and no later evaluation runs earlier than an earlier
356	   one. `CLOCK-REGRESSION` (W < F) and `TRUST.FLOOR_AHEAD_OF_WALL`
357	   (F > W + 90 d) are findings with remedies. L advances to A when A > L. The
358	   anchor is rewritten when continuity is unavailable, within tolerance, or
359	   excused by a witness.
360	
361	Consequences. An accidental forward wall is accepted only up to 90 d beyond
362	signed evidence, so a wrong write is bounded and heals as signed time catches
363	up; a larger jump writes nothing. Expiry, staleness and future checks still
364	fail closed at tEval. Repeated reboots cannot lower F or freeze payload
365	freshness: F only rises, and freshness is evaluated at tEval ≥ F. Report-only
366	evaluation (doctor) computes the same decision, states and findings, labels
367	`evaluationMode: report-only`, and returns `writes: []` with every write field
368	null; it cannot create a recovery challenge.

422	Threat statement. The wall is untrusted. The single-boot, 24 h monotonic
423	challenge window plus the ±24 h issue skew mean that no response to an old
424	challenge, held indefinitely, can later lower the floor to a stale real time:
425	after a reboot or after the window the response is dead, and inside the window
426	the signed time must sit within a day of the wall the operator is looking at.
427	This bounds a signed epoch relative to the wall; it does not prove the wall.
428	The protocol promises install binding (nonce + record digest), single use,
429	serial monotonicity, exact counter preservation and no floor below L. It makes
430	**no promise against a malicious publisher**: a recovery authority that signs a
431	false time is outside the protocol, exactly as it is for every other signed
432	time in this contract. Why this cannot revive revoked trust: revocation is by
433	counter and entries, which the epoch may not change; a key revoked before the
434	epoch cannot sign it; expiry is re-evaluated at signed real time, which is ≥
435	every earlier signed time, so a document genuinely expired at real time stays
436	expired. If the recovery authority is unavailable, recovery is impossible and
437	the install must be re-established by fresh install or authenticated adoption.

441	## S5. Root chain through expired roots (AR-05)
442	
443	An install holding accepted root N evaluates a chain N+1..M link by link. Each
444	link needs the previous root's threshold from that root's keys (continuity)
445	**and** the new root's threshold from its own keys (possession), revoked keys
446	excluded from both. Semantic admission per link: reader supports the schema;
447	version and previous-version contiguity; not issued before its predecessor;
448	issue before expiry; root key policy. Intermediate expiry is never consulted;
449	the final root must be unexpired at tEval and not issued more than 24 h after
450	the wall. Any refusal leaves state unchanged and names the link. Success
451	advances the root counter to M and L to the final root's issue time. An expired
452	root with no chain refuses `ROOT.EXPIRED_NO_CHAIN` with the remedy of presenting
453	a payload carrying N+1..newest. Schema-1 readers refuse a schema-2 root as
454	`ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` (typed, not corruption, state unchanged).

456	## S6. Live revocation (AR-05)
457	
458	Trust epoch `{rootVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, revocationVersion,
459	permissionPolicyDigest}` is captured at operation start. **Authority
460	checkpoint:** every brokered effect request re-reads the epoch under the
461	journal append lock before its intent record. **Observer:** a tick every 5 s
462	reads the counter; if the last successful read is older than 10 s or the read
463	fails, the observer appends `REV(observer-fail-stop)` and cancels. These bounds
464	are implementation qualification obligations under OS scheduling assumptions
465	using `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` (Linux) / `mach_continuous_time` (macOS); they are not a
466	wall-clock guarantee inside a stopped process. A stopped process emits no
467	effects; on resume its first checkpoint or tick observes the stall and fail-
468	stops before any further effect.
469	
470	The observation predicate revokes on a higher counter whose entries name the
471	closure (release, signing key, namespace, catalog snapshot) or on a policy
472	digest change that removes a required grant; unrelated changes are recorded as
473	drift; a lower counter never revokes (rollback is detected by the floor rules).
474	
475	**Linearization** is under the single journal append lock: after `REV` no
476	`RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended, and no brokered effect commits.
477	Commit records carry `postimageSha256`. At `REV(trust-revoked)` the host
478	attempts rollback of reversible completed effects **only where the current
479	bytes equal the committed postimage**; a mismatch is `rollbackBlocked`
480	(user-modified since commit, never overwritten), an unreadable target is
481	`indeterminate`. Irreversible completed effects and effects under
482	`REV(policy|operator)` are disclosed as completed. The `CLN` record lists every
483	residual. Cancellation is bounded: refuse further requests (0 s), protocol
484	Cancel (2 s), SIGTERM (3 s), SIGKILL of the process group and reap (5 s),
485	scratch cleanup under the lease; total 10 s under the same qualification
486	standing. **Unconfined children** (repository code under S10) are not brokered
487	effects: they are cancelled within the bound and disclosed, and their external
488	effects before the kill are not enumerable. No confinement is claimed.
489	
490	**Three different SEAL boundaries, not one.** (1) `linearize` is an abstract
491	brokered-effect schedule over a grant journal. Its all-zero `run3:` SEAL id is
492	a **fixture** token for that schedule. It is not a product host, not native
493	fact authority, and not `identity-model.v3.close_run`. (2)
494	`admit_seal_run_id_prefix` is narrow `run3` pattern dispatch. It admits a
495	well-formed non-fixture prefix and refuses `run2` and the fixture id. It does
496	not replay a graph. (3) `admit_analysis_seal` is the public reference SEAL of
497	an analysis Run: current `JournalRecord` fields (`recordSchema` 3, closed
498	required members), then `identity-model.v3.close_run` on the supplied retained
499	graph, then byte-equal RunId comparison. Owner-only `open_run_closure` is not
500	that boundary. A well-formed `run3:` that is not the replayed identity refuses
501	`SEAL_RUN_ID_MISMATCH`. Schema-2 journals remain frozen historical bytes and
502	are not read as 3. Mixed prefixes refuse. There is no `run[23]` alternation.
503	Revocation still blocks schedule-SEAL after `REV`. Grant/root schema-2
504	documents are a different axis. This dispatch does not change lease modes,
505	lock order, or permission-truth-table effect values. Proof
506	`executionInputsDigest` is required by identity reconstruct; this unit does
507	not mint it.
508	
509	**Commit-admission gate (one atomic bit state).** `ADMITTED = 1`, `LATCHED = 2`: `0` is
510	preparing, `1` admitted, `2` latched before admission, `3` admitted then latched. Commit
511	admission is a compare-exchange `0 → 1`; the observer always fetch-ORs `2`, including
512	`1 → 3`, so a post-admission latch cannot be lost. No state resets during the attempt. A
513	successful gate mints one internal single-use permit for the already prepared commit and is
514	not a reusable grant for later effects. A latch winning at state `0` prevents the gate
515	entirely. State `3` does **not** revoke the already admitted attempt or relabel its outcome:
516	it records the latch and forbids further effect admission or retries. The observer bound
517	bounds admitting new effects; it cannot abort an in-flight syscall or rewrite its outcome. A
518	confirmed durable commit stays committed; an uncertain commit or barrier stays
519	durability-undetermined with its ExecutionId and no automatic write retry. The gate orders
520	admission only and is not the durability point.
521	
522	**`REV` after `SEAL` is not a refusal.** The linearization law above constrains one
523	direction only: after `REV` no `RA`, intent, commit or `SEAL` is appended. It does not follow
524	that a `REV` appearing later in sequence order refuses an earlier `SEAL`. Durable commitment
525	is established solely by the guarded evidence-ledger receipt and its private association. A
526	reader must not infer refusal from record order, and no member is added to the closed
527	schema-3 `JournalRecord` to carry that correlation: the private association and the
528	`AttemptCustodyV1` `executionId ↔ operationRef` mapping (identity §2) are its lawful home.
529	
530	**A receipt present before its attempt is settled is lawful.** Because the settle write is
531	ordered after the receipt write, every committing attempt passes through an interval in which
532	a valid joined receipt exists while the private attempt row is still `admitted`. That is not
533	a contradiction and not a custody condition: the receipt establishes historical commitment,
534	pending settlement is disclosed operationally, and no authority is revived. No writer may
535	reopen a stopped session merely to settle it; settlement is the separately authorized sweep.
536	
537	**Required delivery is a separate phase.** On any end path security returns a stopped
538	cleanup-only session. Required rendering and delivery draw no authority from it: they are a
539	read-and-materialise activity in `SHARED-READ` mode (S7), not a brokered effect. The handoff
540	is: cleanup `REV`/`CLN` through a fresh lawful level-3 then level-4 append while the stopped
541	session still holds the operation lease; release the lease; ordinary S7 end handoff; then a
542	new `SHARED-READ` phase over the committed snapshot. A latched attempt (state `2` or `3`)
543	starts no delivery phase and cannot reacquire authority that way; for state `3` the commit
544	stays committed with its RunId observable and the required delivery is reported failed
545	through the existing `DELIVERY.REQUIRED_FAILED` path. This is the **selected** law, not an
546	open choice.
547	
548	**Publication does not overwrite the workflow outcome.** A successful publication does not
549	force `success` at exit 0. A Run that publishes and then fails its policy assessment
550	terminates `policy-failed` at exit 1 carrying that committed `runId`; a Run whose verdict is
551	indeterminate terminates `indeterminate` at exit 3 carrying its `reasonCodes`. An optional
552	surface failure is disclosed without rewriting either, and `success` can carry neither an
553	`errorCode` nor `reasonCodes`, so no lawful reset to success exists. Required delivery
554	failure is the one lawful class change, and it preserves the RunId.
555	
556	**Carrier anchor bound (selected limit).** No current owner asserts cryptographic
557	authentication of the interior journal prefix. The v8 closed witness member `bodySha256`
558	names the tail body digest, so it detects no interior substitution, and the inherited chain
559	value binds only the immediately previous body digest and index. Confirming a retained
560	carrier therefore establishes presence, contiguity and non-rollback below the last observed
561	operation boundary, under the conclusion class `confirmed-under-retained-custody`. An unmet
562	anchor is reported unknown, never as invalidation. This is a selected compatibility and
563	security limit with a recorded disposition, not an open defect, and the historical v1 prose
564	noted in S1 is not a current claim to the contrary.

566	## S7. Leases and lock order (AR-14)
567	
568	The current security schema bundle declares every array's `x-opensip-order`
569	under identity §3. Namespace lists use strictly unique raw UTF-8 locator order;
570	execution-grant owner records use strictly unique `ownerKey` order. Public code
571	sets use strictly unique UTF-8 order. Other arrays are explicit sequences unless
572	their owning schema states a stricter order: journal revisions, lock traces,
573	release steps, signature entries and observations are never silently sorted.
574	This collection-admission law does not change the security metadata canonical
575	profile or its immutable historical schemas.
576	
577	| Level | Lock | Carrier | Blocking |
578	|---|---|---|---|
579	| 0 | lifecycle fence | `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`, flock LOCK_EX | bounded wait 5 s, then `PROJECT.BUSY` |
580	| 1 | project writer lease | `<namespace>/writer.lease`, LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB | never |
581	| 2 | project reader lease | `<namespace>/readers.lease`, LOCK_SH\|LOCK_NB (readers); LOCK_EX\|LOCK_NB (EXCLUSIVE) | never |
582	| 3 | ledger transaction | SQLite WAL; writers BEGIN IMMEDIATE, busy_timeout 0; readers read a committed snapshot | never for readers |
583	| 4 | journal append lock | in-process mutex | bounded, in-process |
584	
585	Modes: `SHARED-READ` (any number; queries, rendering, doctor, read-only
586	agents), `APPEND-WRITE` (one; analysis, import, baseline pin; publishes only
587	new immutable objects and ledger rows, never deletes or rewrites bytes a reader
588	may reference), `EXCLUSIVE` (GC, purge, migration, repair apply; nothing else
589	held). Readers never block a writer; a second writer or an EXCLUSIVE request
590	gets `PROJECT.BUSY` at once, releases the fence, and may retry outside the
591	fence with backoff 1/2/4/8/15 s within a 30 s budget. Laws: no lease without
592	the fence; no waiting for a lease; no waiting for the fence while holding a
593	lease (operation end releases the lease first); no upgrade; trust state is
594	written only under the fence and never under a lease; GC census is a
595	LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe under the fence and a busy probe means retain.
596	
597	**One-writer refinement (identity-and-evidence §5).** "Exactly one per-project
598	writer holds the lifecycle lease through admission, evaluation and commit" is
599	the APPEND-WRITE mode: exactly one append writer, coexisting with any number of
600	immutable-snapshot readers that never wait on it. The EXCLUSIVE mode is the
601	refinement for migration, purge, GC and repair apply, which need a reader
602	census (the LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB probe) because they may remove or rewrite bytes a
603	reader could reference. There is no contradiction with the identity contract:
604	readers are invisible to the writer's commit order and the writer is invisible
605	to readers' snapshots. Exact selectors: `<namespace>/writer.lease` LOCK_EX|NB
606	is the identity contract's "lifecycle lease"; `<namespace>/readers.lease`
607	LOCK_SH|NB is its "consistent committed snapshot"; `<installRoot>/lifecycle.fence`
608	is its "global trust admission and revocation lock order".
609	
610	**Namespaces.** Every project lease names a namespace from the host namespace
611	registry (ProjectId ↔ namespace locator, identity §5); a lease on an
612	unregistered namespace is a violation, never an implicit registration
613	(`lease-on-an-unregistered-namespace-is-refused-negative`). Namespaces are
614	independent: a writer in one never blocks a writer in another.
615	
616	**Core-transition lock set (decided; SHOULD-6).** `core update|repair|rollback`
617	and `store migrate|rollback` change install-level state, while EXCLUSIVE is a
618	per-namespace lease. The mechanism is a composition, not a new flock mode:
619	
620	1. The install-wide fence (level 0) is held for the **whole** transition, not
621	   only for lease acquisition; no project operation can be admitted meanwhile.
622	2. The affected namespace set is enumerated from the registry by
623	   `core_transition_affected_namespaces` (never from user input or a directory
624	   listing): **all registered namespaces** when the from/to state schema differ
625	   or a store is re-selected (`core rollback`, `store migrate|rollback`);
626	   **no namespace** for a same-schema `core update` or `core repair`, because
627	   the selected core closure is an immutable generation, running project
628	   operations keep their pinned generation and re-check trust at their S6
629	   checkpoints, and nothing they reference is rewritten.
630	3. EXCLUSIVE is taken on each affected namespace in namespace-locator byte
631	   order, non-blocking and all-or-nothing: the first busy namespace releases
632	   every acquired lease in reverse order, releases the fence, reports
633	   `PROJECT.BUSY` naming that namespace and its holders, and the retry is the
634	   ordinary backoff outside the fence.
635	4. The `InstallationTransitionJournalV1` (S9.2) names the exact lease set and is
636	   written only after every lease is held: in the lock model the
637	   `transition-journal` action is lawful only under the fence, only after
638	   `core-transition-acquire` succeeded, and only naming exactly the held set
639	   (`transition-journal-*` cases). Crash
640	   recovery runs as the first act under the next fence acquisition, before any
641	   admission, over the S9.2 recovery table (which defers to the S9 footprint
642	   table for store operations), and re-acquires exactly the journaled
643	   set; flock leases die with the process, so no stale lease survives. A
644	   namespace registered after the intent cannot exist (registration needs the
645	   fence); finding one is `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`.
646	5. Leases are released in reverse order, then the fence. The fence cannot be

722	## S9. Stage transition, schema bridge and floor continuity (AR-14)
723	
724	Bridge. Stage 1: root readers {1}, state decoder v1, TR-REPAIR typed absence,
725	`kernelAttestationKeys` empty. Stage 2: root readers {1, 2}, state decoders
726	`state-decoder.v1` (read-only migration source) and `state-decoder.v2`
727	(writer); schema-2 roots may carry an active TR-REPAIR (threshold ≥ 2, keys ≥

729	attestation keys (no reuse of root keys). Ordered release: (1) the stage-2 core
730	ships under the schema-1 catalog, so every stage-1 install updates by its
731	ordinary path; (2) root N+1 with schema 2 is signed by root-N keys and its own
732	keys; (3) stage-1 cores refuse N+1 typed and keep N until it expires; stage-2
733	cores accept it by the dual reader; (4) state migration 1→2 runs under
734	EXCLUSIVE. Both stages keep the metadata profile of S2.
735	
736	**Physical carrier bridge (carrierFormat).** The project grant-journal carrier has its
737	own format axis, and it is not the state schema. Detection on open is by schema
738	introspection only, because the oldest format carries no version row: object names
739	first, then refusal on a partial set, then definition validation, and the published
740	`carrier_format` row read **last**. Reader staging mirrors the root-reader and
741	state-decoder pattern, and its scope is stated precisely: a **carrierFormat-aware** core
742	that supports only {1, 2} refuses a carrierFormat 3 carrier **typed** and keeps its prior
743	generation until it expires; a carrierFormat {1, 2, 3} core reads both, under
744	recordSchema-1 semantics for historical generations and recordSchema-3 for current ones.
745	A **format-unaware** core cannot be made to refuse at all, because it never looks for
746	`carrier_format`; that limitation is selected and disclosed, detectable but not
747	preventable, and a generation at or above `first_generation` appearing in the inherited
748	table is a split-brain custody condition, never valid history. Its mitigation is the
749	existing ordered-release discipline. A historical `platform` value is surfaced as a
750	historical alias and is never presented as an S8 machine id, rewritten, or joined to
751	`RepoExecutionGrantV2.platformId`. An unmigrated carrier stays fully READABLE for its
752	existing generations, but it cannot admit a schema-3 `SEAL`, so an attempt needing to
753	seal there refuses with the carrier-incompatibility standing until migration completes.
754	
755	**Carrier migration is NOT an installation transition.** It does not use the S9.2 intent
756	or journal, and it cannot: reusing the closed logical `store-migrate` intent with an
757	unchanged state schema and store generation refuses
758	`TRANSITION.MIGRATE_REQUIRES_SCHEMA_ADVANCE` and
759	`TRANSITION.SCHEMA_CHANGE_SELECTS_NEW_STORE`, and an invented `carrier-migrate` operation
760	refuses `TRANSITION.OPERATION`. `InstallationTransitionIntentV1` is a closed 11-member
761	record and `InstallationTransitionJournalV1` a closed 20-member record; neither has a
762	carrier field. Migration 1 or 2 → 3 is instead a **selected prospective expansion** of
763	the existing `store-gc` operation (security-owned, `authorizationClass:
764	exclusive-lease`, `writesTrackedIntent: false`): the inherited row shows only that
765	`store-gc` is not an intent-writing transition, not that this mutation was already
766	authorized, so the added per-namespace behaviour is selected here explicitly. It runs
767	under the install fence with non-blocking `EXCLUSIVE` on
768	the affected project namespace, where a busy namespace is skipped and retained exactly as
769	GC already behaves. Its state is reported through the existing `store-status`
770	`migration-state` field. It is additive, disables no inherited constraint or trigger, and
771	rewrites no inherited row. Three atomic durable acts in order — `TERMINAL` append, object
772	creation, format-row publication — with the format ROW as the commit point and detection
773	keyed on that row, so every durable prefix has an exact resume action. Protocol:
774	`design-corrections/security/carrier-migration.v1.md`. A format-unaware core cannot be
775	made to refuse a migrated carrier, so a generation at or above `first_generation`
776	appearing in the inherited table is a detectable split-brain custody condition, never
777	valid history; the mitigation is the existing ordered-release pattern.
778	
779	**Grant-generation closure gains a third cause.** The inherited rule (security v8 §5.4
780	WA-13, retained unchanged as historical text) advances `grantGeneration` only on
781	whole-generation `REV` and on the uint53 rollover. Carrier-format migration is a third
782	cause of generation closure. It reuses the existing typed `TERMINAL` cause
783	`grantGenerationClosure` and changes no schema, enum or wire major. Floors copy forward
784	unchanged and a poisoned floor is not lowered; only S4.5 lowers it.
785	
786	Migration writes a `migrating` root: PREPARING → PREPARED → (old store fenced
787	`RESTORED`) → COMMITTED → final rename. Recovery from the durable footprint
788	only: absent = nothing to do; PREPARING or PREPARED with the old store unfenced
789	= abort; PREPARED with the old store fenced = resume from step 3; COMMITTED =
790	resume the final rename; final and migrating coexisting, or unknown state =
791	quarantine `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`. Floors (`rootVersion`, `indexSnapshotVersion`,
792	`revocationVersion`, `evalHighWater`, `lastAccepted`, `recoveryEpochSerial`)
793	copy forward into the new store; the boot anchor and any pending challenge do
794	not; roles re-establish by the PRESENT event over the embedded chain. A new core
795	whose embedded chain does not reach the accepted root refuses
796	`ROOT.FLOOR_ABOVE_CORE`. Rollback inside the 30 d window re-selects the retained
797	old store with floors set to the maximum of both stores; it refuses when the
798	new store accepted a root the old core cannot verify (schema or chain reach). A
799	poisoned floor is not lowered by migration or rollback; only S4.5 lowers it.

865	`core update|repair|rollback` and `store migrate|rollback` are five operations
866	of **one** installation transition protocol (S7 lock set, S9 store footprint,
867	S15 command grammar). One closed intent contract and one closed journal record
868	serve all five; the reference is `admit_transition_intent`,
869	`transition_journal_record`, `admit_transition_journal`,
870	`recover_transition_journal` (fixture `transition-journal-cases.v1.json`).

872	**Intent (`InstallationTransitionIntentV1`, the required field contract of the
873	workflow `CoreTransitionIntentV1` successor).** Eleven fields, host-projected,
874	never caller-authored: `schemaVersion` 1; `operation` (the five above);
875	`fromCoreClosure`/`toCoreClosure` (`closure2:`); `fromStateSchema`/`toStateSchema`
876	(1 | 2); `fromStoreGeneration`/`toStoreGeneration` (the selected state-store
877	generation); `platformProfileSetBodyDigest`; `preconditionGeneration` (the
878	observed core generation); `rollbackDeadline` (host-observed, or `null`). The
879	raw SHA-256 of the canonical intent is the mutation step's
880	`inputDescriptorDigest` (S15) and the journal's `intentDigest`. Semantics,
881	total over the shape: `core-repair` keeps closure, schema and store; `core-update`
882	changes the closure, never lowers the schema, selects a new store generation
883	exactly when the schema changes; `core-rollback` changes the closure, never raises
884	the schema, needs the deadline; `store-migrate` keeps the core closure, advances
885	the schema and selects a new store generation; `store-rollback` keeps the core
886	closure, retreats the schema, re-selects the retained generation, needs the
887	deadline. An earlier revision recorded that "the current nine-field, three-operation workflow
888	schema cannot express a store operation" and owed the workflow owner an enum extension. **That is
889	discharged in current bytes:** `workflows/schemas/invocation-record.schema.json#/$defs/
890	CoreTransitionIntentV1` now requires all eleven fields, including `fromStoreGeneration` and
891	`toStoreGeneration`, and its `operation` enum is the five operations above. The successor field
892	contract and the workflow schema agree, and `integration-host-model.py` validates one intent against
893	both (`CoreTransitionIntentV1` then `InstallationTransitionIntentV1`) before
894	`admit_transition_intent`. The retained `nine-field-legacy-intent-*` case keeps its meaning: a
895	nine-field intent is refused, which is now a regression against a schema that no longer produces one.
