898	For `core-update` and `core-rollback` alike, an unchanged state schema keeps the
899	store generation (`TRANSITION.SAME_SCHEMA_KEEPS_STORE`) and a changed state
900	schema selects a different one (`TRANSITION.SCHEMA_CHANGE_SELECTS_NEW_STORE`).
901	`core-repair` keeps closure, schema and store together. `store-migrate` requires
902	an advanced schema **and** a different generation; `store-rollback` requires a
903	retreated schema **and** a different generation. No admitted intent changes the
904	store generation with an unchanged schema, and the S9 footprint above already
905	owns the re-selection of a retained store. This restates exactly what

907	
908	**Journal (`InstallationTransitionJournalV1`; identity
909	`H("security.installation-transition-journal.v1", record)`).** Written under the
910	held fence, only after every lease of the affected set is held (`fenceHeld` and
911	`writtenAfterAllLeasesHeld` are schema constants), in state `LEASED`. It binds:
912	the `intentDigest` and every intent field; the namespace registry frozen under
913	the fence (`registry`, `registryDigest`); `affects` and the exact `leaseSet`,
914	which must equal `core_transition_affected_namespaces` over that frozen
915	registry (a caller cannot choose a smaller or different set: `TRANSITION.SCOPE_MISMATCH`);
916	and, through admission, the current state schema, store generation and core
917	generation the transition starts from. Admission context (all host observations
918	under the fence): `intent`, `intentDigest`, `namespaceRegistry`, `fenceHeld`,
919	`leasesHeld` (what the S7 composition actually acquired), `currentStateSchema`,
920	`currentStoreGeneration`, `currentCoreGeneration`, `admittedTime`. Refusals
921	`TRANSITION.*` (D9 `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`): among them
922	`LEASE_SET_NOT_HELD` (a busy namespace means no journal is written),
923	`FENCE_NOT_HELD`, `INTENT_DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `INTENT_FIELD_MISMATCH:<f>`,
924	`REGISTRY_MISMATCH`, `CURRENT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH`, `CURRENT_STORE_MISMATCH`,
925	`PRECONDITION_GENERATION_MISMATCH`, `ROLLBACK_WINDOW_EXPIRED`,
926	`NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT` (rollbacks need an S4 admitted time inside the
927	host-observed window; user arguments cannot extend it). States: `LEASED →
928	PREPARING → PREPARED → COMMITTED → DONE`, or `ABORTED`.
929	
930	**Crash recovery (`recover_transition_journal`), the first act under the next
931	fence, before any project admission.** Fail closed: no fence → refuse; a
932	registry that differs from the frozen one → `QUARANTINE` / `MIGRATION.CORRUPT`
933	(registration needs the fence, so the footprint is ambiguous); the journaled
934	lease set not re-acquired exactly → `PROJECT.BUSY` (retry outside the fence);
935	then by state: `LEASED`/`PREPARING` → `ABORT` (nothing selected; installation
936	unchanged); `PREPARED` → a store operation follows the S9 footprint table
937	(`RESUME-COMMIT` from step 3 only when the old store is fenced `RESTORED`,
938	otherwise `ABORT`; no footprint → `QUARANTINE`), a core operation aborts (the
939	published generation was never selected; GC census reclaims it); `COMMITTED` →
940	`RESUME-COMMIT` (a committed transition is finished, never reversed, even after
941	the rollback window); `DONE`/`ABORTED` → release only. Cases `crash-at-*`,
942	`registry-changed-*`, `journaled-lease-set-not-exactly-reacquired-*`.
943	
944	### S9.3 Private store-instance lineage (successor; proposed, not accepted)
945	
946	A numeric store generation is not unique over time: `store-rollback` re-selects a
947	retained generation and `core-rollback` never raises the schema, so two physically
948	distinct stores can present the same `(storeGeneration, stateSchema)` pair. A
949	private **store instance identity** disambiguates them for local operational
950	records. It adds no member to `InstallationTransitionIntentV1`,
951	`InstallationTransitionJournalV1`, the namespace registry or any signed document,
952	introduces no envelope kind and no public major, and mints no D9 class, code or
953	exit; its refusals are the existing `TRANSITION.*` set and the existing
954	`MIGRATION.CORRUPT` quarantine. It is never a wire field, an authority token or a
955	semantic input, and it never enters the pure evaluator or a Run hash.
956	
957	**Instance identity.** Each physical store instance carries one `storeInstanceId`:
958	32 lowercase hexadecimal characters from 128 bits of OS CSPRNG, allocated once
959	when that store is created, persisted in that store's own root before the store is
960	first published, and never rewritten. It has no ordering and no arithmetic, and
961	reading it grants nothing.
962	
963	**Lineage nodes, identified by the full triple.** A private append-only table
964	holds one node per admitted binding triple
965	`(storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema)`, carrying its predecessor triple
966	and the `intentDigest` of the transition that created it; both are `null` exactly
967	at a **lineage root**. Every lookup uses the whole triple, whose instance component
968	is read from the store-root **marker** of the store concerned: a numeric pair alone
969	never identifies a node, because a retained branch may lawfully present the same
970	pair as a fresh target. `intentDigest` is evidence validated *on* the selected node
971	and is never a search key, since it may lawfully repeat. This section asserts no
972	global uniqueness of a store generation beyond what the rules above already impose.
973	
974	**Marker observation is three-way and phase-bound.** Reading a store root yields
975	exactly one of: a **readable** identity; **absent**, meaning no store root is
976	present; or **unreadable**, meaning a root was observed but its marker is missing
977	or malformed. An unreadable marker is never treated as absence, and an absence must
978	be observed, never inferred from a missing observation. The store a transition
979	comes from always exists, so its marker is always required. The **selected**
980	store's marker is required only where the transition is settled as committed: at
981	`LEASED` and `PREPARING` a forward selection's target may not yet be materialised,
982	and after an abort an unpublished target may already have been reclaimed by the GC
983	census, so an absent target there is expected and must never be read as corruption.
984	
985	**One admission law.** A node is admitted only if its shape is admitted by the
986	private record's own closed schema, its predecessor and origin digest are null
987	together or present together, it does not name its own triple, its non-null
988	predecessor already exists as a node at that exact triple, no existing node shares
989	its primary key with disagreeing contents, and the chain from it is acyclic and
990	reaches exactly **one** lineage root. That root rule is scoped to the chain, not to
991	the whole table: an authorized restore or adoption starts its own lineage, so
992	several lineages may coexist. Publication and recovery apply this same law, and an
993	exact byte-identical match at the target key is idempotent but **not** a short
994	circuit — it is validated the same way and simply writes nothing. A refusal writes
995	nothing.
996	
997	**Selection case, derived from the admitted intent alone.** By the pair law in
998	S9.2 the case is decidable without reading any stored node: equal `to`/`from`
999	generation and schema is a **same-store** selection; an advanced schema is a
1000	**forward selection**; a retreated schema is an **ancestor re-selection**. Only a
1001	forward selection materialises a new store, allocates a fresh `storeInstanceId`
1002	and writes one node, after the journal record is durably `COMMITTED` and never
1003	inside a level-4 grant-journal append lock. A same-store or ancestor re-selection
1004	writes no node: the store it selects already has one, created by an earlier act.
1005	
1006	**Recovery applies the same case, and only after the owner decides.**
1007	`recover_transition_journal` keeps every decision it already makes; this adds no
1008	state, code or recovery action, and in particular a core operation at `PREPARED`
1009	still aborts and a store operation still follows the S9 footprint. Where that
1010	function refuses, reports the project busy or quarantines, the companion makes **no
1011	decision at all**, inspects nothing and reads no marker. Where its action settles
1012	the transition as committed — `RESUME-COMMIT` or `RELEASE-ONLY` reaching `DONE` —
1013	then: a **forward selection** node must be present at its own full triple, or else
1014	reconstructed from the journal record's own from/to generation and schema members
1015	together with the predecessor and selected store-root markers, and admitted by the
1016	law above. A **same-store or ancestor** re-selection validates the retained node at
1017	its own full triple and **never rewrites its predecessor or origin digest**; an
1018	ancestor must additionally lie on the verified chain from the current node, so a
1019	store at a merely equal numeric pair off that chain never qualifies. That node was
1020	created by an earlier, unrelated act whose origin the current intent does not carry,
1021	so a missing one cannot be repaired from it and is `QUARANTINE` /
1022	`MIGRATION.CORRUPT`. No atomicity is claimed between the journal record and a node.
1023	
1024	**Before the owner settles a transition**, pre-existing ancestry is expected and
1025	untouched, including a retained branch at the same numeric generation, and an
1026	absent target is expected as above. Where a target *is* observable, what must not
1027	exist is a *new* node for that transition at **its own full triple**. For a forward
1028	selection, any node at that new target triple is premature. For a same-store or
1029	ancestor re-selection, the pre-existing node is expected; only a node claiming the
1030	current unrelated transition as its origin is contradictory. Each is a premature-node contradiction
1031	and quarantines; ordinary pre-existing lineage remains unchanged.
1032	
1033	**Lineage roots.** A root is created by an authorized local act that materialises a
1034	new physical store outside any transition: installation, or an authorized evidence
1035	restore or portable adoption. Such an act allocates a fresh `storeInstanceId`,
1036	**replaces** any marker present in copied bytes before first publication so a
1037	restored store never impersonates its source, imports no node from the source, and
1038	imports no floor, grant or local commit authority. No transition is invented to
1039	give it an `intentDigest`.
1040	
1041	**Floors and authority are unchanged by this section.** An authorized transition
1042	keeps the S9 floor rules exactly: migration copies the floors forward into the new
1043	store, rollback inside the window sets them to the maximum of both stores, and a
1044	poisoned floor is lowered only by S4.5. An instance identity records which physical
1045	store is selected; it never lowers a floor and never confers local commit authority.
1046	
1047	## S10. Execution principal `repository-code`
1048	
1049	Principal classes: `first-party`, `repository-code`, `imported-artifact`.
1050	Repository execution is disabled by default. The display names are aliases of
1051	one foundation semantic-grant principal kind: workflow `P-TRUSTED-REPO` and
1052	native `repository-code` both map to `trusted-repository-code`
1053	(identity-schemas.v3 `semantic-grant`). Two identities are kept apart: the
1054	foundation `semanticGrantDigest` (semantic projection inside plan2: principal
1055	kind, closure, owner-source digest, operations, scope; no nonce, expiry or
1056	consent) and the operational `securityGrantRef` =
1057	`H("security.repo-execution-grant.v2", grant)` under the product canonicalizer
1058	(this record). The workflow `TestExecutionStepParams.authorizationRef` and the
1059	native `AuthorizedExecutionV2.authorization` both reference the operational
1060	identity.
1061	
1062	A `RepoExecutionGrantV2` (supersedes the never-accepted V1 draft, retained in
1063	the bundle as superseded) is admitted only when: schema 2; principal
1064	`repository-code`, `semanticPrincipalKind` `trusted-repository-code`;
1065	projectId, snapshotId (`snapshot2:`) and argv digest equal the invocation's;
1066	execution class in {build-script, proc-macro, test-runner}; **owners** (≤ 64,
1067	unique) each bind `{ownerKey, source, ownerFileManifestSha256}` where `source`
1068	is `snapshot-member` (validated against the sealed snapshot's owner manifests)
1069	or `dependency-closure-member` (validated against the **sealed
1070	`DependencySourceSetV1`**, whose id must equal `dependencySourceSetId`) — so
1071	build scripts and proc-macros of external crates are grantable exactly when
1072	they are in the sealed closure, never from an ambient registry or vendor
1073	directory; `ownerSourceDigest` equals the host-computed owner-set digest; the
1074	**runner** is a
1075	member of the sealed first-party tool closure (`toolClosureId`, `closure2:`;
1076	bundled cargo/rustc/linker/test runner) for build-script and proc-macro, or a
1077	tool-closure member or sealed snapshot member for test-runner — there is no
1078	system cargo, rustc, linker or shell fallback; `platformId` is one of the four
1079	S8 machine platform ids (a display alias refuses); every effect value (`subprocess`, `filesystemWrite`,
1080	`network`, `environment`) **equals** the security owner's platform truth
1081	table entry (currently `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`,
1082	`ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` on all four platforms; a stronger or weaker claim
1083	refuses). Those four effect *names* are copied from four of the seven closed
1084	permission **tokens** in `permission-truth-tables.v9.json`, and the
1085	correspondence — `subprocess`→`PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED`,
1086	`filesystemWrite`→`PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE`, `network`→`PT-NET-EGRESS`,
1087	`environment`→`PT-ENV-READ`, with the values read from the `child-process`
1088	execution mode these owners run in — is tabulated in native §5.2. Two limits
1089	carry with it: `PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` names the **host's own state store**, so
1090	neither the token nor a grant over it confers authority over the repository
1091	filesystem — its `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` value states that nothing prevents writes
1092	anywhere, since the code holds the invoking user's ambient authority; and
1093	`PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED`, the one token whose value is
1094	`ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER`, is deliberately projected by no effect name, because
1095	repository code here is not routed through a host broker. Confinement remains
1096	never claimed; authorization is `interactive-explicit` (never in CI) or
1097	`policy-record` with a record id; the grant's `ci` flag is a real boolean equal
1098	to the invocation's; the project policy admits the principal; expiry is
1099	operation-end; not inherited. The native contract copies these effect values
1100	into `AuthorizedExecutionV2.effects` and its `owners[]` are this grant's
1101	owners; the workflow contract's `consentSource` (`pre-existing-policy` |
1102	`interactive-consent`) maps to `policy-record` | `interactive-explicit`, and
1103	its `argv0Source` maps to `runner`. Revocation of a running grant is the S6
1104	path; confinement is never claimed.
1105	
1106	**Operational admission precedes any Plan (decided; SHOULD-2).** A grant
1107	authorizes one *operational* step: native preparation (build-script /
1108	proc-macro owners, workflow `native prepare`) or a workflow test-execution step
1109	(test-runner). Preparation runs before the analysis Plan that will consume its
1110	outputs exists, and a test-execution step has no Plan at all (workflows §1/§7),
1111	so **no Plan semantic-grant projection is an admission input** of
1112	`admit_repo_execution_grant`; a ctx projection supplied beside the grant is not
1113	read (`a-ctx-projection-is-never-consulted-not-an-authority-condition`), and a
1114	host must not fabricate one from the grant. The bindings that hold every grant
1115	are the ones listed above: project, snapshot, argv digest, execution class,
1116	owners (preparation classes), runner, tool closure, platform and truth-table
1117	effects, consent, `ci`, expiry, non-inheritance, and the S6 live boundaries
1118	during the step. For a test-runner grant `owners` is `[]` and
1119	`ownerSourceDigest` is the digest of the canonical empty owner array
1120	(`4f53cda1…2b945`): canonical empty-set bookkeeping that keeps the record
1121	shape uniform and binds nothing; the runner is bound by `runner` +
1122	`toolClosureId`/snapshot membership + `argvDigest`
1123	(`test-runner-grant-admits-with-no-plan-*`,
1124	`test-runner-runner-outside-both-sealed-sets-refuses-although-the-empty-owner-digest-matches`).
1125	
1126	The Plan-time join is separate and later. `semantic_projection_for_grants`
1127	lists the `trusted-repository-code` principals (`{kind, closureId,
1128	ownerSourceDigest}`) of the **preparation** grants whose prepared outputs an
1129	analysis consumes; a test-runner grant contributes nothing, because its
1130	evidence enters a Plan only as an `import2` payload whose wrapper and
1131	test-execution step receipt retain the operational `securityGrantRef`. When the
1132	analysis is admitted, `admit_plan_execution_projection(planPrincipals,
1133	consumedGrants, preparedResolution)` requires, under `host-prepared`, that the
1134	plan2 semantic-grant projects exactly those principals
1135	(`PLAN.EXECUTION_PRINCIPAL_NOT_PROJECTED:<digest>` /
1136	`PLAN.PROJECTED_PRINCIPAL_WITHOUT_GRANT:<digest>`), refuses any
1137	`trusted-repository-code` principal under `imported-inert` or `none` (prepared
1138	availability never implies this host held a grant), and refuses a test-runner
1139	grant offered as a consumed grant (`PLAN.TEST_RUNNER_HAS_NO_PLAN`). The
1140	projection comes from the Plan and the grants from the step receipts; they must
1141	agree, and neither is derived from the other. D9: `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
1142	(request-rejected 2). Records `SemanticProjectionV1`,
1143	`ExecutionProjectionAdmissionV1`; cases `plan-*`,
1144	`semantic-projection-for-grants-*`. **Implemented, not owed:**
1145	`integration-host-model.py` derives the Plan requirement through
1146	`semantic_projection_for_grants(grants)` and `check-integration.py` drops
1147	`ctx.semanticGrantPrincipals` before operational admission and then checks the Plan-time join
1148	(`consuming-plan-preparation-principal-join`, `consuming-plan-missing-principal-refused`,
1149	`imported-inert-does-not-infer-local-grant`, `test-runner-is-operational-not-a-plan-principal`,
1150	`test-runner-cannot-be-consumed-as-preparation`).
1151	
1152	### S10.1 Repair apply authorization (not a repository-execution grant)
1153	
1154	Repair apply is host-brokered **first-party** source mutation: the host writes
1155	postimages it computed from a signed recipe closure under the EXCLUSIVE lease.
1156	No repository code runs. Its authorization is therefore a separate record,
1157	`RepairApplyAuthorizationV1` (product data; identity
1158	`H("security.repair-apply-authorization.v1", record)` is the workflow
1159	`RepairApplyParams.authorizationRef`), admitted only when: projectId,
1160	`repairPlanId` (`repairplan2:`) and `baseSnapshotId` (`snapshot2:`) equal the
1161	invocation's; the live tree still equals the base snapshot
1162	(`AUTHZ.SOURCE_MOVED`); `recipeClosureId` (`closure2:`) equals the recipe in
1163	the rehashed repair plan (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_MISMATCH`) and is positively
1164	admitted under current signed-closure trust (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_NOT_ADMITTED`).
1165	Absence from the revocation set is insufficient. Revocation refuses first
1166	(`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, D9
1167	`EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`); consent is `interactive-explicit` (never in
1168	CI) or `policy-record`, with a real boolean `ci` equal to the invocation's;
1169	expiry operation-end; `leaseMode` `EXCLUSIVE`; `repositoryExecution` is the
1170	constant `false` and cannot be set. Live revocation: every brokered write
1171	passes the S6 authority checkpoint; a revoked recipe closure at any checkpoint
1172	is `REV(trust-revoked)` with postimage-checked rollback and the workflow's
1173	`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK` / `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` states. Reference
1174	`admit_repair_authorization`; fixture `repair-authorization-cases.v1.json`.
1175	
1176	Fingerprint-targeted repair consumes `finding-key2` fingerprints of **finding3**
1177	occurrences on a **run3** evidence Run (workflow evaluator3 repair descriptor
1178	`evidenceRunId`). The fingerprint domain stays `finding-key2`; that is
1179	correspondence identity, not a finding2 occurrence and not a run2 graph.

1188	### S10.2 Repair recovery authorization (decided; post-reset v2 N-4/P9)
1189	
1190	Recovery inspection (`repair recover` without `--apply-recovery`, workflows §6
1191	`repair_inspect`) is read-only and needs no authorization. Every recovery
1192	**mutation** (`discard-temps`, `roll-back-renamed`,
1193	`verify-postimages-and-commit`) is a separately authorized host-brokered
1194	write within the **original** plan's authority, under the EXCLUSIVE lease, and
1195	its authorization is the closed security record `RepairRecoveryAuthorizationV1`
1196	(product data; identity `H("security.repair-recovery-authorization.v1", record)`
1197	is the workflow `RepairApplyJournalV1.recoveryAuthorizationRef`, always the full
1198	reference, never a truncated prefix). It is admitted by
1199	`admit_recovery_authorization(authz, ctx)` only when every binding holds:
1200	
1201	- **Project, plan, snapshot, recipe.** `projectId`, `repairPlanId`,
1202	  `baseSnapshotId` and `recipeClosureId` equal the admitted project and the
1203	  rehashed original plan (`AUTHZ.*_MISMATCH`).
1204	- **Exact journal identity (noncircular).** `journalRef` =
1205	  `security.repair-apply-journal-identity.v1:` + `H` over the closed identity
1206	  preimage `{schemaFamily, schemaMajor, requestId, stepId, executionId,
1207	  repairPlanId, baseSnapshotId, authorizationRef}`: only fields fixed when the
1208	  apply journal was created, never `state`, paths, blobs, blocked/restore lists
1209	  or any `recoveryAuthorizationRef` the journal later carries, so one journal
1210	  has one identity in every state and the reference written into the journal
1211	  never enters its own preimage (`journal-identity-mismatch-*`,
1212	  `journal-of-a-different-plan-*`).
1213	- **Observed journal state and replay/crash semantics.** `journalState` and
1214	  `observedJournalStateDigest` (raw SHA-256 of canonical `{state, stagedPaths,
1215	  appliedPaths, preimageBlobs}`) equal the journal **as read under the EXCLUSIVE
1216	  lease before any recovery write**. Every successful recovery mutation changes
1217	  `state`, so a retained authorization cannot be replayed after one
1218	  (`AUTHZ.JOURNAL_STATE_MOVED`; `replay-after-a-successful-rollback-*`); a crash
1219	  or a `requires-broker` return before the first write leaves the digest
1220	  unchanged. The same authorization may continue only within the same still-admitted
1221	  recovery execution and lifetime. A process crash ends that execution; a fresh
1222	  attempt requires a newly admitted authorization bound to its new execution id (`crash-before-the-first-recovery-write-*`).
1223	- **Finite action.** `recoveryAction` equals the one the journal state admits
1224	  (`PREPARING`/`STAGED` → `discard-temps`; `APPLYING` → `roll-back-renamed`;
1225	  `APPLIED`/`INDETERMINATE` → `verify-postimages-and-commit`;
1226	  `AUTHZ.RECOVERY_ACTION_MISMATCH` otherwise). Terminal states (`COMMITTED`,
1227	  `FAILED_*`, `RECOVERY_BLOCKED`) admit no mutation
1228	  (`AUTHZ.RECOVERY_NOT_MUTATING:<state>`); the table mirrors the workflow
1229	  recovery table's mutating rows, and the integration checker asserts that equality today
1230	  (`security-workflow-recovery-action-table-identical`, comparing the mutating rows of
1231	  `W.RECOVERY_TABLE` with `S.RECOVERY_ACTION_FOR_STATE`).
1232	- **Fresh attempt.** `originalRequestId` equals the journal's `requestId`;
1233	  `recoveryRequestId`/`recoveryExecutionId` equal the recovery invocation's own
1234	  ids and differ from the original (`AUTHZ.RECOVERY_REQUEST_NOT_FRESH`).
1235	- **Consent and policy.** Consent is `interactive-explicit` (never in CI) or
1236	  `policy-record`, with a real boolean `ci` equal to the invocation's; the project
1237	  policy admits repair.
1238	- **Time.** `issuedAt` ≤ S4 admitted evaluation time ≤ `expiresAt`, lifetime at
1239	  most 24 h; no admitted time context refuses (`AUTHZ.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT`).
1240	- **Boundary.** `leaseMode` `EXCLUSIVE`, `mutationBoundary` `host-broker`,
1241	  `repositoryExecution` and `newEdits` are the constant `false`: recovery can
1242	  never grant repository code execution, write a byte the original plan did not
1243	  name, or broaden the plan (`planScope: original-plan-only`).
1244	- **Current host custody.** The S3 custody rule is re-run on the recovery
1245	  invocation (`AUTHZ.CUSTODY_NOT_ADMITTED`); an old admission does not carry over.
1246	
1247	**Safe rollback versus re-executing a revoked recipe.** `discard-temps` and
1248	`roll-back-renamed` restore retained preimages or discard temps and **never
1249	consult recipe trust**: rolling back after the recipe was revoked is exactly what
1250	revocation rollback is (`rollback-recovery-admits-although-the-recipe-closure-is-revoked-*`).
1251	`verify-postimages-and-commit` would commit the recipe's postimages, so it
1252	re-consults current signed-closure trust: a revoked recipe refuses first
1253	(`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, D9 `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`) and a recipe
1254	not positively admitted refuses (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_NOT_ADMITTED`). The
1255	workflow recovery table's guarded preimage/postimage law (every target at its
1256	plan preimage or postimage before any restore or commit; otherwise
1257	`RECOVERY_BLOCKED`) is mandatory and never waived by this record.
1258

1316	### S12.1 Projecting a refusal onto the one closed public detail vocabulary
1317	
1318	A public termination carries exactly one `domainDetail` = `{code, remedy, subject?}`, and `code` is a
1319	member of the single closed registry (`design-corrections/public-detail-registry.v1.json`, mirrored by
1320	`workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/DomainDetailCode`). This section states the projection
1321	this unit's refusals take, so that "detail" in the prose above is never ambiguous between a registry
1322	member and free subject text. Reference `public_detail` / `public_details`, record
1323	`PublicDetailProjectionV1`, fixture `public-detail-cases.v1.json`, sweep
1324	`public-domain-details-are-a-closed-set-with-a-bounded-pending-registration-gap`.
1325	
1326	1. **Base code, then subject.** The base code is everything before the **first** colon; everything
1327	   after it is subject data. `ROOT.ROLE_SET:1` is code `ROOT.ROLE_SET`, subject `1`.
1328	2. **A registered detail wins over the enclosing refusal.** When a refusal carries a `detail` whose
1329	   base code is a registry member, that is the public code. This is why the 38 `ROOT.*` document
1330	   defects are public codes instead of collapsing into one `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE`, and it is
1331	   exactly why `ENVELOPE.*` and `PROFILE_SET.*` belong in the registry: they occupy the same position
1332	   in `admit_profile_set_envelope` that `ROOT.*` occupies in `admit_root_document`, and S9.1 names
1333	   them normatively as `detail`.
1334	3. **Otherwise the refusal supplies the code and the whole detail is subject text.** This is the
1335	   existing reading for `RECOVERY.REFUSED` (`CHALLENGE_EXPIRED`, `COUNTER_MISMATCH:<k>`,
1336	   `ISSUED_TOO_OLD_FOR_WALL`, …), for `CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED` (`SYMLINK`, `WRITABLE_BY_OTHERS`, …)
1337	   and for `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR`, `JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE`, …). Those
1338	   sub-details are deliberately **not** registry members; registering them would create a second
1339	   public vocabulary for the same events.
1340	4. **The vocabulary is closed, not a prefix rule.** The unit declares the exact set it may emit
1341	   (`SECURITY_PUBLIC_DETAIL_CODES`, 191 members). A detail whose base code lies inside one of the
1342	   eight families this unit publishes (`AUTHZ.`, `ENVELOPE.`, `GRANT.`, `NT-TCB-`, `PLAN.`,
1343	   `PROFILE_SET.`, `ROOT.`, `TRANSITION.`) but outside that set **refuses**; there is no open
1344	   `PROFILE_SET.*` wildcard.
1345	5. **The D9 branch comes from the refusal, never from the detail.** Naming a defect more precisely
1346	   never changes its termination branch. `PROFILE_SET.NO_TR_PROFILE_ROLE` therefore travels under
1347	   `ROOT.SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED` → `REQUEST.SCHEMA_MAJOR_UNSUPPORTED` exactly as S9.1 says, while every
1348	   other `PROFILE_SET.*`/`ENVELOPE.*` defect travels under `PAYLOAD-NOT-ADMISSIBLE` →

1335	| Fold | `fold(n)` is Unicode **Default Case Conversion `toLowercase(X)`**: the **full**, **non-tailored**, **context-sensitive** default lowercase mapping (Unicode Standard §3.13 / UAX #21). It is the **same single fold** the honored-`lib` agreement below uses, and this section defines no other: no NFC/NFKC step, no trimming, no alias table, no prefix or suffix matching. Reference implementation `native_evidence_model.v2.lib_name_fold` |
1336	| Mapping | `component(n) = "lib." + fold(n) + ".d.ts"`. Total, deterministic and **one-directional**: a selected name maps to exactly one component basename, and a component is never mapped back into a selected name |
1337	| Membership | for every `n` in `libSelection`, `component(n)` must be an element of the declared `component` set. A name whose component is absent refuses `native.native-context-lib-not-retained:<n>` — §10 route `request-rejected` (2) / `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, before PlanId |
1338	| Equality | `{fold(n) : n ∈ libSelection}` must equal `{fold(m) : m ∈ honoredOptions.lib}`. `honoredOptions.lib` is required and non-empty in the closed resolved context, so this agreement always applies and is **not** weakened by the mapping. Two `libSelection` entries with the same fold refuse `native.native-context-field-mismatch:duplicate-lib-selection`; a set disagreement refuses `native.native-context-field-mismatch:libSelection` |
1339	| Order | `libSelection` is sorted by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the **retained, unfolded** names; `standardLibraryComponentDigests` by the raw UTF-8 bytes of `component`. Each record keeps its own specified order for hashing — folding is a comparison, never a rewrite of a retained value, and neither array is re-spelled into the other's vocabulary |
1340	
1341	**What `fold` is, and what it is not.** The three plausible operations are genuinely different
1342	and only one of them is the one this admission performs, so it is named rather than approximated.
1343	
1344	| Discriminator | `fold` (**full default lowercase**) | simple lowercase | case folding |
1345	|---|---|---|---|
1346	| `U+0130` LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT ABOVE | `U+0069 U+0307` — **two** code points, through `SpecialCasing.txt` | `U+0069`, one code point | `U+0069 U+0307` |
1347	| `U+039F U+03A3` (sigma in **final** position) | `U+03BF U+03C2` — the `Final_Sigma` condition | `U+03BF U+03C3` | `U+03BF U+03C3` |
1348	| `U+03A3 U+039F` (sigma **not** final) | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` | `U+03C3 U+03BF` |
1349	| `U+00DF` LATIN SMALL LETTER SHARP S | `U+00DF` — unchanged | `U+00DF` | `U+0073 U+0073` |
1350	
1351	So `fold` is **not** `Simple_Lowercase_Mapping` (it expands, and it is position-dependent) and
1352	**not** `Case_Folding` (sharp s is unchanged). It is **non-tailored** — the root locale, with no
1353	Turkish/Azeri dotless-i and no Lithuanian tailoring — so the result must never depend on an ambient
1354	locale, an environment variable or a host language setting.
1355	
1356	**Version custody, and the portability consequence it does not hide.** The result of a default case
1357	conversion is determined by the Unicode case data the host carries, so `fold` is deterministic
1358	**given a case-data version**, and this design binds the reference derivation to one:
1359	`native_evidence_model.v2.UNICODE_CASE_DATA_VERSION`, currently **UCD 15.0.0**, the version the
1360	table above was measured against. Two hosts on different case data can fold the same name
1361	differently — for a code point unassigned in one of them (an unassigned code point folds to itself),
1362	or for one whose mapping changed between the versions — and because `libSelection` enters the
1363	context descriptor and therefore `PlanId`, that would be an admission divergence, not a cosmetic
1364	one. This contract does **not** claim the fold is invariant across every runtime. It requires the
1365	version to be a declared, checkable property rather than whatever the runtime happens to ship:
1366	`unicode_case_data_agreement()` reports the running version against the declared one so drift is
1367	disclosed instead of silently changing an outcome. Nothing here narrows the field to ASCII to
1368	sidestep the question — it is simply true that every `lib` name in the pinned compiler's own option
1369	vocabulary is ASCII, where all three operations above coincide, and that is a fact about the current
1370	vocabulary rather than a constraint on the value.
1371	
1372	**Custody: the two arrays answer different questions.** `libSelection` is the
1373	*configuration-facing* record of what the resolved options selected, and it is
1374	what the universe/config agreement is checked against.
1375	`standardLibraryComponentDigests` is the *tree-facing* **complete** declaration
1376	inventory of the retained stdlib closure — one row per `.d.ts` member with its
1377	raw digest, selected or not. So the selection never narrows the inventory and the
1378	inventory never adds a selected name: a missing inventory row refuses
1379	`native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<basename>`, and a tree in
1380	which two paths share a basename refuses
1381	`native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<basename>` — the mapping's
1382	target would not be unique, and an arbitrary resolution is exactly what this
1383	refusal exists to prevent. The join reads **no other input**: not a
1384	caller-supplied map, not a filesystem lookup, not a compiler query, not the
1385	`typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` value on its own.
1386	
1387	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
1388	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
1389	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
1390	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
1391	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
1392	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
1393	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
1394	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
1395	
1396	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
1397	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
1398	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
1399	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
1400	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
1401	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
1402	
1403	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
1404	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
1405	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
1406	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
1407	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
1408	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
1409	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
1410	the admitted id refuse
1411	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
1412	
1413	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
1414	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
1415	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
1416	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
1417	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
1418	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
1419	
1420	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
1421	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
1422	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no duplicate names under the
1423	published `fold`, and selects the same folded name set as the honored `lib` list
1424	— the same `fold` the component join above uses, and the only one this section
1425	defines; each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
1426	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
1427	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
1428	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
1429	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
1430	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
1431	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
1432	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
1433	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
1434	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
1435	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public
1436	DomainDetail codes.
1437	
1438	**Independent derivation (§9.5) applies to TypeScript exactly as to Rust.** The worker
1439	recomputes the context from its own sealed inputs; a differing byte is
1440	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze.

1468	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
1469	
1470	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
1471	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
1472	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
1473	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
1474	
1475	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
1476	
1477	| Field | Rule |
1478	|---|---|
1479	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
1480	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
1481	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
1482	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
1483	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
1484	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
1485	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
1486	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
1487	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
1488	
1489	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
1490	
1491	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
1492	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
1493	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
1494	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
1495	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
1496	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
1497	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
1498	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
1499	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
1500	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
1501	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
1502	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
1503	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
1504	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
1505	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
1506	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
1507	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
1508	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
1509	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
1510	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
1511	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
1512	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
1513	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
1514	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
1515	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
1516	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
1517	  syntax analysis.
1518	
1519	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
1520	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
1521	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
1522	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.
1523	
1524	### 3.2 Custody and transport
1525	
1526	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed
1527	by `fileManifestSha256`; Plan-bound by `dependencySourceSetId`. Transport uses
1528	protocol-3 frames `DependencySourceManifest / DependencySourceChunk /
1529	DependencySourceSeal / DependencySourceAccepted` (§9.2) with the same byte-exact,
1530	digest-verified, reject-before-use discipline as the snapshot. The worker mounts
1531	the accepted files read-only at `.opensip/deps/v1/<name>-<version>/…` in its
1532	private scratch materialization. Nothing is fetched lazily.

1534	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
1535	
1536	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
1537	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
1538	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
1539	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
1540	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
1541	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
1542	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
1543	
1544	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
1545	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
1546	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
1547	
1548	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
1549	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
1550	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a
1551	  silent skip. `ancestorCarrierVerified=true` is recorded in the context.
1552	- **CC-2** `CARGO_HOME` is a fresh private empty directory created for the
1553	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.
1554	- **CC-3** The constructed environment contains no `PATH`, `CARGO_*`, `RUSTFLAGS`,
1555	  `RUSTC*`, `RUSTDOC*`, `RUSTUP_*`, `CC`/`CXX`/`LD`/`AR`/`TARGET_*` variables;
1556	  presence of any is a refusal. Tool locations are passed as absolute closure
1557	  paths on the command line, not via environment.
1558	- **CC-4** Every selected tool digest equals its entry in `ToolClosureV1`.
1559	- **CC-5** Every `.cargo/config(.toml)` inside the snapshot (any directory, not
1560	  only the root) is replaced in the materialization by the single projected file;
1561	  the originals remain snapshot bytes for identity but are never read by Cargo.
1562	
1563	Projected (honored) keys: `build.target`, `build.rustflags`,
1564	`target.<triple>.rustflags` (both through the flag allowlist below),
1565	`source.<name>.directory` pointing inside the snapshot with `replace-with`,

1567	`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `build.rustc-workspace-wrapper`,
1568	`build.rustdoc`, `build.target-dir`, `build.build-dir`, `build.incremental`,
1569	`build.dep-info-basedir`, `cargo-new`, `credential-alias`, `doc`, `env`,

1668	  cause `generated-file-out-of-bounds`), `maxGeneratedFilesPerOwner 4096`,
1669	  `maxGeneratedFileBytes 67108864`, `maxGeneratedTotalBytes 1073741824`,
1670	  `maxGeneratedFileRows 1000000` (protocol limit). Imported blobs are bound to
1671	  archive members by exact `blobs[]` digest; an archive member outside the
1672	  wrapper's `blobs` is never read (`generated-file-path-escape-and-bounds-refused`).
1673	- **PO-1 (staleness)** A row is usable only if `inputBinding` equals the current
1674	  context (owner manifest, dependency set, toolchain digest, cfg set). A stale row
1675	  is refused before Plan construction (`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, detail
1676	  `native.stale-prepared-output`, listing the differing fields) when prepared mode
1677	  was selected explicitly, or is ignored with a disclosed `staleRows` list and
1678	  non-prepared fallback when prepared mode was defaulted. It never uses a stale blob.
1679	- **PO-2 (failed rows)** A `failed` build script is retained as a row so the same
1680	  inputs need not be re-run; the owner is analyzed non-prepared
1681	  (`build-script-generated-unavailable`).
1682	- **PO-3 (imported)** An imported set carries the same binding fields and
1683	  `provenanceAssurance: declared`; the host cannot verify that an external
1684	  preparer produced the expansions faithfully. Facts derived from them are
1685	  Plan-bound and disclosed with the import identity and producer.
1686	
1687	Where do the expansions and generated files come from? From the **preparation
1688	step** (§5.3), which is the only place proc-macro dylibs are built and loaded and
1689	build scripts run, inside the authorized `repository-code` principal with live
1690	boundaries. The step captures the required generated **data** and discards every
1691	executable product; its output is the inert row set, and the worker consumes only
1692	that.
1693	
1694	---
1695	
1696	## 4. Resolution completeness (AR-12)
1697	
1698	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1699	
1700	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1701	
1702	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1703	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1704	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1705	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1706	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1707	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1708	
1709	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1710	
1711	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1712	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1713	
1714	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1715	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1716	
1717	```
1718	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1719	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1720	```
1721	
1722	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1723	`identity-schemas.v3.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1724	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1725	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1726	
1727	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1728	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1729	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1730	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1731	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1732	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1733	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1734	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1735	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1736	
1737	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1738	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1739	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1740	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1741	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1742	against a value the provider never supplied.
1743	
1744	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1745	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1746	
1747	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1748	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1749	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1750	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1751	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1752	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1753	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1754	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1755	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1756	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1757	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1758	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1759	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1760	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema
1761	   DOCUMENT bytes** (§7.2). A caller may restate it but never choose it: a value that is not the
1762	   registered document's digest refuses `native.coverage-payload-schema-not-registered`
1763	   (`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`).
1764	
1765	Every refusal above is `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` (`operational-failed` 4) under the §10
1766	fault law: a worker that lies about its partition contributes no facts, no Coverage and no
1767	Run. This is not a Coverage deficiency; an admitted-but-incomplete input is (§10).
1768	
1769	**Coverage use (`coverage_view_use`).** A `view2` may name a `coverage2` only if that
1770	`coverage2` was admitted at the boundary above and its `scope2` is one of the view's own
1771	`scopeIds`. A hash-valid `coverage2` whose subject scope sits outside the evaluated view is
1772	refused exactly as hidden finding evidence is (identity §3), rather than joined silently.
1773	
1774	**No circularity.** `D` names the snapshot, the universes and the enumerator closure. A
1775	universe descriptor (§2) names its native context, tools and config projection; a native
1776	context names closures; none of them names a scope, a Coverage, a view, an evidence record
1777	or a Run. The derivation order is therefore total and acyclic: closures → native context →
1778	universe → `scope2` → commitment → Coverage payload → `coverage2` → `view2`. The foundation
1779	scope *descriptor* whose raw digest is `scopeDigest` (§1.4, workspace roots and path
1780	prefixes) is a different record with a different job and is not this commitment.
1781	
1782	Cases: `subject-scope-commitment-is-the-scope2-identity-in-native-sha256-text-form`,
1783	`subject-scope-commitment-binds-the-snapshot-not-only-the-subject-list`,
1784	`coverage-admission-mints-coverage2-from-the-host-subject-scope`,
1785	`coverage-commitment-chosen-by-the-claimant-is-refused`,
1786	`coverage-producer-chosen-narrower-examined-partition-is-refused`,
1787	`coverage-examined-subject-count-that-disagrees-with-the-enumeration-is-refused`,
1788	`coverage-key-naming-a-universe-outside-the-host-scope-is-refused`,
1789	`coverage-complete-claimed-over-an-admitted-unresolved-edge-is-refused-at-the-boundary`,
1790	`coverage-incomplete-over-an-exhaustive-partition-admits-with-the-same-commitment`,
1791	`coverage-use-requires-the-subject-scope-to-be-in-the-evaluated-view`,
1792	`coverage2-whose-subject-scope-is-outside-the-view-is-refused`,
1793	`coverage2-never-admitted-at-the-producer-boundary-is-refused-in-a-view`,
1794	`subject-scope-duplicate-subject-refuses-rather-than-silently-deduping`,
1795	`coverage-payload-schema-digest-a-caller-chose-is-refused`. The two positive coverage cases

1797	digest and the canonical payload rather than pinning a literal, so a schema-document edit moves the
1798	identity visibly instead of silently invalidating a frozen value.

2167	### 4.8 Type derivation provenance (feedback 12)
2168	
2169	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
2170	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
2171	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
2172	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
2173	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
2174	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
2175	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
2176	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
2177	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
2178	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
2179	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
2180	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.

2182	**The two clauses have different scopes, and the second is deliberately the wider
2183	one.** The first names the method of `TypeDerivationV1`, whose
2184	`confidenceMillionths` is a schema **constant** `1000000` and whose
2185	`confidenceMethod` is the constant `native.confidence.v1`: that record exists only
2186	on a `types@checked` fact. The second — *no value below 1000000 is produced by a
2187	native provider* — is **not** narrowed to `types@checked`. It is a **provider
2188	emission law** over this whole bundle: no native provider of any relation emits a
2189	confidence below 1000000, because a native fact is exact under its admitted
2190	universe and this design publishes no calibrated probability for any relation. It
2191	is not read as types-scoped, and reading it that way would be a *weakening* — it
2192	would permit a native `clones` or `references` provider to emit a fabricated
2193	percentage, which is exactly what §4.8 removed.

2221	test-runner`). One principal, three current spellings, joined explicitly and

2243	to analyze; OpenSIP does not vouch for it and does not confine it unless a

2248	
2249	Domain `native.authorized-execution.v2`. Closed descriptor bound into
2250	`rust-v2.executionCapableResolution` via `preparedOutputSetId`: `{schemaVersion:2,
2251	operation:"native.prepare", principalClass:"repository-code", projectId,
2252	snapshotId (snapshot2), dependencySourceSetId, toolchain, toolClosure, cfgSetId,
2253	owners: [{ownerKey, kind: build-script|proc-macro, ownerFileManifestSha256,
2254	provenanceAssurance: registry-authenticated|declared|in-snapshot}], effects:
2255	{subprocess, filesystemWrite, network, environment: {requested, enforcement}},
2256	authorization: {mode: interactive-explicit|policy-record, policyRecordId|null, ci},
2257	liveBoundaries: {revocationCheck: before-each-owner, cancellation:

2260	`EnforcementV1` values are **copied from the security owner's platform truth
2261	table**; this contract never asserts an `ENFORCED-PLATFORM` value itself, and the
2262	model refuses a record that claims more than the pinned table (`permission-truth-tables.v9.json`:
2263	`network`/`subprocess`/`filesystemWrite` `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`; `environment`
2264	`ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION`).
2265	
2266	**Which token each effect name is copied from (CB4-ADV-3).** The four effect
2267	names here are `effects` field names; the pinned table is over seven closed
2268	permission **tokens**, and the correspondence was determinate by elimination but
2269	published nowhere, so an implementer had to infer it. It is stated:
2270	
2271	| `effects` field | Permission token | `ENFORCED` in v9 (child-process) | What the value means |
2272	|---|---|---|---|
2273	| `subprocess` | `PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | No mechanism prevents the effect; the record states what was asked and answered. |
2274	| `filesystemWrite` | `PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | Same. See the scope note below. |
2275	| `network` | `PT-NET-EGRESS` | `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` | Same. |
2276	| `environment` | `PT-ENV-READ` | `ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` | The child's environment is constructed by the host, so the capability is never conferred *in this execution mode*. |
2277	
2278	Three scope facts travel with that table and none of them may be dropped:
2279	
2280	1. **The values are per execution mode.** `native.prepare` runs owners as child
2281	   processes, so the `child-process` column is the applicable one. In v9's
2282	   `in-host-process` mode *every* token including `PT-ENV-READ` is
2283	   `DISCLOSURE-ONLY`, because a component sharing the host's address space shares
2284	   its environment. Quoting `ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION` without its mode would
2285	   over-claim.
2286	2. **`PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE` is not repository filesystem authority.** The token
2287	   names the *host's own state store*. Neither it nor any grant over it confers
2288	   authority over the repository tree, and its `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` value says
2289	   precisely that nothing prevents writes anywhere: the executing code holds the
2290	   invoking user's ambient authority throughout. `filesystemWrite` here is a
2291	   disclosure of that fact, never a scoping of it.
2292	3. **`PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED` is deliberately unprojected.** It is the one token
2293	   whose v9 value is `ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER`, and no `effects` field carries
2294	   it, because repository code under `native.prepare` is not routed through a
2295	   host broker. `EnforcementV1` admits the value, so the vocabulary is not
2296	   narrowed; nothing in this contract claims it. The two read-only tokens
2297	   (`PT-FS-READ-PROJECT`, `PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT`) are likewise unprojected: they
2298	   are not effects this record authorizes.

2318	
2319	Owned by the host resolved-inputs adapter (never the semantic worker), after
2320	snapshot seal and dependency-source admission, before PlanId:
2321	
2322	1. Verify the carrier (§3.3 CC-1..CC-5); materialize snapshot and dependency
2323	   sources read-only in private scratch; write the single projected
2324	   `.cargo/config.toml`; construct the environment.
2325	2. Check current trust and revocation state (security owner's clock), then for
2326	   each owner in order: re-check revocation (`before-each-owner`), run the bundled
2327	   Cargo to compile and execute the build script or to build the proc-macro crate
2328	   for the selected cfg set (`cargo check --offline --frozen --locked --target
2329	   <triple>` restricted to the owners; the linker used is the closure linker;
2330	   nothing is installed).

2332	   through the closure proc-macro server for every invocation site in the
2333	   workspace and dependency crates that names one of the built proc-macro crates,

2335	   `cargo:` directive output as `build-script-directives` rows. Loading the
2336	   proc-macro dylib *is* executing repository code; it happens here, under the

2340	   `build-script-directives` row; capture as `generated-file` rows the regular
2341	   data files under `OUT_DIR` named by the crate's
2342	   `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))` sites when
2343	   those are statically determinable, else every regular data file under

2383	
2384	### 6.1 Modes and evidence levels
2385	
2386	| Mode | Level/algorithm | Evidence level (closed) | Authority |
2387	|---|---|---|---|
2388	| `exact` | `L0-verbatim` | `byte-identical` | fact |
2389	| `normalized` | `L1-lexical` (default) or `L2-comment-insensitive` (opt-in) | `lexically-identical` / `comment-insensitive-identical` | fact |

2391	| `near` | `near-v1`: Jaccard over 5-gram shingles of the L3 token stream | `similar-candidate` | candidate only |
2392	| `cross-tsjs` | `tsjs-erasure-v1` projection, then L3 | `cross-language-syntax-candidate` / `excluded` | candidate only |
2393	
2394	No semantic equivalence is inferred by any mode.

2396	### 6.2 Parameters (selected)
2397	
2398	`minOccurrences 2`; `minBodyBytes 64` (exact); `minTokens 20` (L1–L3,
2399	cross-tsjs); `minTokens 50` (near); `nearThreshold 800000` millionths;
2400	`maxCandidatesPerGroup 4096`; `maxGroupsPerUniverse 1000000`.

2402	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
2403	
2404	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
2405	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
2406	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
2407	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
2408	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
2409	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
2410	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
2411	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
2412	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
2413	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
2414	
2415	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
2416	|---|---|---|---|
2417	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
2418	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
2419	
2420	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
2421	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
2422	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.

2424	### 6.4 TS/JS cross-language decision (feedback 9)
2425	
2426	Decision: `languageId` **stays** in exact fact identities (a `.ts` and a `.js`
2427	body are different facts). Cross-TS/JS matching is a separate **candidate-only**
2428	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
2429	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:
2430	
2431	- Removed before L3 normalization: type annotations, `type`/`interface`
2432	  declarations, type parameter lists, `as` assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`,
2433	  definite-assignment `!`, `declare`/`readonly`/`abstract`/access modifiers,
2434	  `implements` clauses, `import type`/`export type`.

2436	  `enum`/`const enum`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`),
2437	  value-bearing `namespace`, decorators, `import =`. A body containing any of them
2438	  is **excluded** from cross matching with reason

2441	  `semanticEquivalenceClaimed=false`, `automaticDeletionEligible=false` as schema

2615	`plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`, and `coverage-v3`.

2619	payload is FactBatchV3. When absent, historical FactBatchV2 remains and

2624	companions are bounded by existing `maxFactBatchCandidates` (4096) and

2630	   identity tokens are required for every worker; a row lacking any of them, or
2631	   any token the Plan needs, is never spawned: affected Coverage keys are

2633	   `snapshot2`, `plan2` or source byte reaches a worker that cannot name them

2636	   array and identity versions; mismatch → `FAULT`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`,

2650	
2651	| Frame | Direction | Payload | Terminal |
2652	|---|---|---|---|

3489	`edition` is a map from crate **name** to year, so it is the *selected value*
3490	that is the dialect, never the map: a body identity that varied with unrelated
3491	crates would be neither meaningful nor representable. When the map's distinct
3492	value set has exactly one member — the ordinary case, including a large
3493	single-edition workspace — that member is the dialect of every body and no owner
3494	selection arises. When it has more than one, the **owning compilation unit
3495	decides**.

3497	More precisely, the **compilation target** decides, not the package. Cargo
3498	documents an `edition` on a target that **defaults to** `package.edition` when
3499	absent — `cargo metadata` lists `targets[].edition` and states the package value
3500	is a default individual targets may differ from, and the `[[bin]]`/`[lib]`
3501	`edition` field, though deprecated, is still documented. So *source → package →
3502	package edition* misses a supported override, and a universe whose package
3503	defaults **all agree** can still contain a target that does not. There is
3504	therefore **no single-edition fast path**: a `clones` fact over a Rust universe
3505	requires the committed ownership relation whatever the package map looks like,
3506	and a null `sourceUnitOwnershipId` admits no clone.

3509	`RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.sourceUnitOwnershipId` is the `h-identity` of
3510	`native.source-unit-ownership.v1` that carries it — required and nullable,
3511	exactly as `preparedOutputSetId` is. It holds three things:
3512	
3513	- `units` — the **closed table of compilation targets**:
3514	  `{unitId, markerPath, crateName, targetKind, targetName, targetEdition}`.
3515	  `targetEdition` is the target's own edition when it sets one and `null` when it
3516	  takes the package default, so the two committed places can never contradict.
3517	- `selectedUnitIds` — the **explicit analysis scope**, non-empty, every member a
3518	  declared `unitId`.
3519	- `ownership` — the pure relation `{path, unitId}`, carrying no edition and no
3520	  metadata, so it cannot contradict the table.

3522	`unitId` is **derived, never declared**:
3523	
3524	```
3525	unitId = H(native.compilation-unit.v1,
3526	           UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion: 1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName})
3527	```

3529	carried as `sha256:<64 hex>`, with **`derived` retention**: nothing separate is
3530	retained, because the preimage *is* the unit row, and admission re-derives and
3531	compares (`sourceUnitOwnership.unitId`). **This is not an opaque digest** — the
3532	preimage record, its domain, its codec and its selector are all published here,
3533	so any consumer rebuilds it from the row that carries it.

3535	An earlier draft joined the fields with delimiters,
3536	`markerPath#targetKind:targetName`. **That is withdrawn.** It was injective only
3537	by excluding `#` from `markerPath`, and a `#` in a repository directory is
3538	admissible under the canonical repository-path contract — so the recipe narrowed
3539	admitted paths in order to make a delimiter work, which is the wrong trade. `H`
3540	needs no such restriction, is fixed width for every admitted path and name
3541	length, and a marker under a `#`-containing directory closes a complete Run.
3542	
3543	`units` is strictly unique by `unitId`, and `unitId` is a function of the
3544	metadata, so **two contradictory rows for one purported unit are a refusal, never
3545	two units that differ by accident**, and a selection or ownership row naming an
3546	undeclared `unitId` is an unbound caller label and inadmissible.
3547	
3548	`markerPath` is the inventoried manifest that declares the target — the same
3549	vocabulary `WorkspaceUnitV2` already uses, under the ordinary canonical
3550	repository-path admission with no added restriction. **`WorkspaceUnitV2` and
3551	`UnitMembershipV1` cannot supply this binding**, and that is a granularity
3552	statement rather than an oversight: they identify *workspace* units
3553	(`cargo-package`, `cargo-workspace`), while one package holds several targets
3554	that may carry different editions. Naming the marker joins my targets to that
3555	existing discovery vocabulary instead of competing with it.
3556	
3557	**Because the selection is committed inside the record whose `h-identity` the
3558	universe names, a different selection is a different record, a different identity
3559	and therefore a different `sourceUniverse`.** That is what makes the required case
3560	representable: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is
3561	validly analysed **under each selection, one at a time**, each with its own
3562	correct dialect and its own body identity, and **no relation payload changed** to
3563	make it so.
3564	
3565	Selection is exact and total, and the order of decision is fixed so each step has
3566	its own cause. No committed ownership refuses. `enumeration: partial` refuses
3567	**before any row is read**. Rows are those whose `path` **equals** the enclosing
3568	fact's anchor path — never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first
3569	match — and no row at all refuses as not-compiled. Rows are then restricted to
3570	`selectedUnitIds`, and a path compiled only by **unselected** targets refuses as
3571	not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition. Selected owners whose
3572	effective editions **agree** are admissible — the ordinary shared-file and
3573	lib-plus-test-target case. Selected owners that **disagree** are an ambiguous
3574	unselected request and refuse. §2.1's retained-input admission independently
3575	requires every marker and owned path to be a source of the same snapshot, every
3576	selection and ownership row to name a declared unit, and every deferring unit to
3577	name a crate the same `edition` map declares.
3578	
3579	**Selected scope is not incomplete enumeration.** A selection says these targets
3580	*are* the analysis, so an owner outside them is deliberately out of scope; it is
3581	committed in the identity, so every consumer sees it and it changes the universe.
3582	`partial` says the producer did not finish, so an owner *inside* the selected
3583	scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one — a gap in
3584	knowledge, invisible as a selection, admitting no dialect at all. Silently
3585	omitting a conflicting owner from the table is not a selection either: an
3586	omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity.
3587	Partial evidence stays useful under the existing law rather than voiding a Run —
3588	the clones scope mints no body identity, its Coverage carries the incompleteness,
3589	and the predicate and seal are indeterminate.
3590	
3591	The consequence is the one that matters: an **ordinary mixed-edition workspace
3592	has a representable valid form**. Each path is owned by units of one edition, so
3593	bodies of *both* editions are admissible in the *same* universe, each carrying
3594	its own dialect. Only a path genuinely compiled under two different editions
3595	refuses, which is a real ambiguity in the input rather than a gap in the law.
3596	This record states what a producer claims it enumerated; it admits no compiler,
3597	measures no build and qualifies no enumerator.
3598
